notes.1: (sn): The third year of the reign of Jehoiakim would be ca. 605 B.C. At this time Daniel would have been a teenager. The reference to Jehoiakim’s third year poses a serious crux interpretum, since elsewhere these events are linked to his fourth year (Jer 25:1; cf. 2 Kgs 24:1; 2 Chr 36:5-8). Apparently Daniel is following an accession year chronology, whereby the first partial year of a king’s reign was reckoned as the accession year rather than as the first year of his reign. Jeremiah, on the other hand, is following a nonaccession year chronology, whereby the accession year is reckoned as the first year of the king’s reign. In that case, the conflict is only superficial. Most modern scholars, however, have concluded that Daniel is historically inaccurate here.
notes.2: (sn): King Nebuchadnezzar ruled Babylon from ca. 605-562 B.C.
notes.3: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.4: (sn): This attack culminated in the first of three major deportations of Jews to Babylon. The second one occurred in 597 B.C. and included among many other Jewish captives the prophet Ezekiel. The third deportation occurred in 586 B.C., at which time the temple and the city of Jerusalem were thoroughly destroyed.

rashi.heb:
*בשנת שלוש למלכות יהויקים.* 
וכי אפשר לומר כן והלא הוא מלך בשנת ד' ליהויקים שנאמר (ירמיהו כ״ה:א׳) בשנה הד' ליהויקים בן יאשיהו מלך יהודה היא השנה הראשונה לנבוכדנאצר ומה ת"ל בשנת שלש בשנת שלש למרדו שנאמר (מלכים ב כ״ד:א׳) ויהי לו יהויקים עבד שלש שנים וישב וימרד בו שלש שנים ובשנת שלש עלה עליו והיא שנת שמונה לנבוכדנצר דאמר מר שנה ראשונה כבש ננוה שניה עלה וכבש יהויקים ושלש שנים עבדו ושלש שנים מרד בו והיא היתה שנת אחת עשרה למלכות יהויקים חמש שנים קודם שכבשו ושלש שעבדו ושלשה שמרד בו ואז מת יהויקים תחת ידו והמליך נבוכדנצר תחתיו יהויכין בנו:
rashi.eng: *In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim.* Now is it possible to say so? Did he [Nebuchadnezzar] not reign in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, as is stated (Jer. 25:1) “in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah that is the first year of Nebuchadnezzar?” So what is the meaning of “In the third year?” In the third year of his rebellion, as is stated (II Kings 24:1): “and Jehoiakim was his vassal for three years; then he turned and rebelled against him;” and in the third year, he overcame him, and that was the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar, for the master said (Seder Olam ch. 24): In his first year he conquered Nineveh, and in his second year he advanced and vanquished Jehoiakim, who served him for three years and rebelled against him for three years. That was the eleventh year of the reign of Jehoiakim: five years before he vanquished him, three years that he served him, and three years that he rebelled against him. And then Jehoiakim died under his hand, and in his stead, Nebuchadnezzar enthroned Jehoiachin, his son.

notes.5: (tn): The Hebrew term translated “Lord” here is אֲדֹנָי (’adonay).
notes.7: (tn, Heb): “hand,” which is often used idiomatically for one’s power and authority. See BDB 390 s.v. יָד 2.
notes.10: (sn, Heb): The land of Babylonia ( “the land of Shinar”) is another name for Sumer and Akkad, where Babylon was located (cf. Gen 10:10; 11:2; 14:1, 9; Josh 7:21; Isa 11:11; Zech 5:11).
notes.11: (tn): Or “gods” (NCV, NRSV, TEV; also later in this verse). The Hebrew term can be used as a numerical plural for many gods or as a plural of majesty for one particular god. Since Nebuchadnezzar was a polytheist, it is not clear if the reference here is to many gods or one particular deity. The plural of majesty, while normally used for Israel’s God, is occasionally used of foreign gods (cf. BDB 43 s.v. אֱלֹהִים 1, 2). See Judg 11:24 (of the Moabite god Chemosh); 1 Sam 5:7 (of the Philistine god Dagon); 1 Kgs 11:33 (of the Canaanite goddess Astarte, the Moabite god Chemosh, and the Ammonite god Milcom); 2 Kgs 19:37 (of the Assyrian god Nisroch). Since gods normally had their own individual temples, Dan 1:2 probably refers to a particular deity, perhaps Marduk, the supreme god of Babylon, or Marduk’s son Nabu, after whom Nebuchadnezzar was named. The name Nebuchadnezzar means “Nabu has protected the son who will inherit” (HALOT 660 s.v. נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּר). For a discussion of how temples functioned in Babylonian religion see H. Ringgren, Religions of the Ancient Near East, 77-81.
notes.12: (tn, Heb): “brought.” Though the Hebrew verb “brought” is repeated in this verse, the translation uses “brought…put” for stylistic variation.

rashi.heb:
*ומקצת כלי בית האלהים.* 
לקח ומקצתם נשארו כמו שנאמר (ירמיהו כ״ז:י״ט) כה אמר ה' צבאות אל העמודים ועל הים ועל המכונות ועל יתר הכלים הנותרים בעיר הזאת:
rashi.eng: *and some of the vessels of the House of God.* he took, and some of them remained, as is stated (in Jeremiah 27:19): “so has the Lord of Hosts said concerning the pillars, concerning the sea, concerning the bases, and concerning the rest of the vessels, which Nebuchadnezzar did not take into exile (sic).”

rashi.heb:
*ויביאם ארץ שנער בית אלהיו.* 
לקלס לעבודת כוכבים שלו הביא שם את השביה כולה אף את האנשים ואת הכלים הביא אח"כ בית האוצר:
rashi.eng: *and he brought them to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god.* to praise his idols; he brought the entire captivity there, even the people, and the vessels he brought afterwards to the treasury.

notes.14: (sn): It is possible that the word Ashpenaz is not a proper name at all, but a general term for “innkeeper.” See J. J. Collins, Daniel (Hermeneia), 127, n. 9. However, the ancient versions understand the term to be a name, and the present translation (along with most English versions) understands the word in this way.
notes.15: (sn): The word court official (Hebrew saris) need not mean “eunuch” in a technical sense (see Gen 37:36, where the term refers to Potiphar, who had a wife), although in the case of the book of Daniel there was in Jewish literature a common tradition to that effect. On the OT usage of this word see HALOT 769-70 s.v. סָרֹיס.
notes.17: (tn, Heb): “and from the seed of royalty and from the nobles.”

rashi.heb:
*הפרתמים.* 
דוכסים:
rashi.eng: *the nobles.* Heb. הַפַּרְתְּמִים, dukes.

notes.22: (tn, Heb): “to stand in the palace of the king.” Cf. vv. 5, 19.
notes.23: (sn): The language of the Chaldeans referred to here is Akkadian, an East Semitic cuneiform language.
notes.24: (tn, Heb): “Chaldeans” (so KJV, NAB, NASB, NRSV). This is an ancient name for the Babylonians.

rashi.heb:
*ואשר כח בהם.* 
פירשו רז"ל שיהיו אונסין עצמן מן השחוק ומן השיחה ומן השינה מפני אימת מלכות ושמעמידים עצמן כשנצרכים לנקביהם:
rashi.eng: *and who have strength.* Our Sages explained (Sanh. 93b) that they should restrain themselves from laughing, speaking and sleeping, out of fear of the throne, and resist the urge when they feel the need to relieve themselves.

rashi.heb:
*וללמדם ספר.* 
מוסב על אשר כח בהם:
rashi.eng: *and to teach them the script.* This refers back to “who have strength.”

notes.25: (tn, Heb): “a thing of a day in its day.”
notes.26: (tn, Heb): “from the delicacies of the king.”
notes.27: (tn): Or “educated.” See HALOT 179 s.v. I גדל.

rashi.heb:
*וימן.* 
ל' הזמנה:
rashi.eng: *allotted.* Heb. וַיְמַן, an expression of preparation.

rashi.heb:
*מפת בג.* 
הוא שם מאכל המלך בל' כשדים ויש פותרים פת בג לחם ואין נראה כן שהרי כתיב ויהי המלצר נושא את פת בגם ונותן להם זרעונים ואין זרעונים חליפי לחם אלא חליפי תבשיל:
rashi.eng: *of… food.* Heb. מִפַּתבַּג. That is the name of the king’s fare in the language of the Chaldeans. Some interpret פַּתבַּג, [as] bread, but it does not appear correct, for it is written (below verse 16): “The steward would take away פַּתבָּגָם … and give them pulse.” Now pulse is not a substitute for bread, but a substitute for cooked food.

notes.30: (tn, Heb): “among them”; the referent (the young men taken captive from Judah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.32: (sn): The names reflect a Jewish heritage. In Hebrew Daniel means “God is my judge”; Hananiah means “the Lord is gracious”; Mishael means “who is what God is?”; Azariah means “the Lord has helped.”

notes.33: (tc): The LXX and Vulgate lack the verb here.
notes.34: (sn): The meanings of the Babylonian names are more conjectural than is the case with the Hebrew names. The probable etymologies are as follows: Belteshazzar means “protect his life,” although the MT vocalization may suggest “Belti, protect the king” (cf. Dan 4:8); Shadrach perhaps means “command of Aku”; Meshach is of uncertain meaning; Abednego means “servant of Nego.” Assigning Babylonian names to the Hebrew youths may have been an attempt to erase from their memory their Israelite heritage.

rashi.heb:
*בלטשאצר.* 
על שם עבודת כוכבים של בבל שקרויה בל שנאמר די שמיה בלטשאצר כשום אלהי, בלטשאצר שם ל' חכמה בל' ארמי:
rashi.eng: *Belteshazzar.* He named him after the god of Babylon, which was called Bel, as it is said (4:5): “whose name is Belteshazzar, like the name of my god.” Teshazzar is the Aramaic expression denoting wisdom.

notes.36: (tn): Or “would not make himself ceremonially unclean”; TEV “become ritually unclean.” Various reasons have been suggested as to why such food would defile Daniel. Perhaps it had to do with violations of Mosaic law with regard to unclean foods, or perhaps it had to do with such food having been offered to idols. Daniel’s practice in this regard is strikingly different from that of Esther, who was able successfully to conceal her Jewish identity.
notes.37: (tn, Heb): “with the delicacies of the king and with the wine of his drinking.”

rashi.heb:
*יתגאל.* 
ל' לכלוך:
rashi.eng: *not to be defiled.* Heb. לֹא יָתְגָּאַל, an expression of sullying.

notes.38: (tn, Heb): “Then God granted Daniel loyal love and compassion before the overseer of the court officials.” The expression “loyal love and compassion” is a hendiadys; the two words combine to express one idea.

rashi.heb:
*שר הסריסים.* 
שהיה שר על משרתי המלך:
rashi.eng: *the chief officer.* who was the chief over the king’s servants.

notes.39: (tn, Heb): “The overseer of the court officials.” The subject has been specified in the translation for the sake of clarity.
notes.41: (tn, Heb): “Why should he see your faces thin from the young men who are according to your age?” The term translated “thin” occurs only here and in Gen 40:6, where it appears to refer to a dejected facial expression. The word is related to an Arabic root meaning “be weak.” See HALOT 277 s.v. II זעף.
notes.42: (tn): The words “if that happened” are not in the Hebrew text but have been added in the translation for clarity.
notes.43: (tn, Heb): “my head.” Presumably this is an implicit reference to capital punishment (cf. NCV, TEV, CEV, NLT), although this is not entirely clear.

rashi.heb:
*אשר מנה.* 
אשר הזמין וסיפק:
rashi.eng: *who allotted.* who prepared and provided.

rashi.heb:
*כגילכם.* 
דוגמתכם ולשון משנה הוא בן גילו:
rashi.eng: *like you.* כְּגִילְכֶם, of your likeness. It is the language of the Mishnah; one of his likeness.

rashi.heb:
*וחיבתם את ראשי למלך.* 
תגרמו לי להתחייב להתיז ראשי:
rashi.eng: *and you will forfeit my head to the king.* You shall bring about that I will be condemned to be beheaded.

notes.44: (sn): Having failed to convince the overseer, Daniel sought the favor of the warden whom the overseer had appointed to care for the young men.

rashi.heb:
*המלצר.* 
הסודר את המנות ואת הקערות שקורין מאישטרי"ב אל"ה:
rashi.eng: *the steward.* Heb. הַמֶּלְצַר, the one who arranges the portions and the plates, called maestre sala, seneschal, steward.

rashi.heb:
*נס.* 
לשון נסיון:
rashi.eng: *test.* Heb. נַס an expression of (נִסָיוֹן) testing.

rashi.heb:
*מן הזרועים.* 
מין קטניות תחת פת בג:
rashi.eng: *some pulse.* a type of beans instead of the food.

notes.45: (tn, Heb): “let our appearance be seen before you.”
notes.47: (tn, Heb): “delicacies of the king.” So also in v. 15.

rashi.heb:
*וכאשר תראה.* 
לפי מה שתראה עשה:
rashi.eng: *and as you will see.* According to what you see, do.

notes.49: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the warden mentioned in v. 11) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.50: (tn, Heb): “listened to them with regard to this matter.”
notes.51: (sn): The number ten is sometimes used in the OT as an ideal number of completeness. Cf. v. 20; Zech 8:23; Rev 2:10.

notes.52: (tn, Heb): “fat of flesh”; KJV, ASV “fatter in flesh”; NASB, NRSV “fatter” (although this is no longer a sign of health in Western culture).

notes.54: (tn): The words “from their diet” are not in the Hebrew text but have been added in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*נושא את פת בגם.* 
נוטלו לעצמו:
rashi.eng: *carry away their food.* He would take it for himself.

notes.55: (tn, Heb): “at the end of the days which the king said to bring them.”

rashi.heb:
*אשר אמר המלך להביאם.* 
שיבאו לפניו:
rashi.eng: *that the king ordered to bring them.* that they come before him.

notes.58: (tc): The MT lacks the conjunction, reading the first word in the phrase as a construct (“wisdom of insight”). While this reading is not impossible, it seems better to follow Theodotion, the Syriac, the Vulgate, and the Sahidic Coptic, all of which have the conjunction.

rashi.heb:
*החרטומי.* 
אלו ששואלי' בטימי מתים בעצמות מתים כמה דאת אמר שחיק עצמות שחיק טמיא:
rashi.eng: *the necromancers.* These are the ones who inquire of טִימֵי מֵתִים, the bones of the dead, as you say, “May his bones be crushed,” שְּׁחִיק טַמַיָא.

rashi.heb:
*האשפים.* 
אלו שדוחקים במזל כך מפורש בתנחומא:
rashi.eng: *the astrologers.* These are the ones who “press” the constellation. So it is explained in Tanhuma (Miketz 2, Buber, Miketz 4).

notes.60: (sn): The Persian king Cyrus’ first year in control of Babylon was 539 B.C. Daniel actually lived beyond the first year of Cyrus, as is clear from 10:1. The purpose of the statement in 1:21 is merely to say that Daniel’s life spanned the entire period of the neo-Babylonian empire. His life span also included the early years of the Persian control of Babylon. However, by that time his age was quite advanced; he probably died sometime in the 530’s B.C.

rashi.heb:
*ויהי דניאל.* 
בגדולה בבבל עד שנת אחת לכורש המלך לדברי האומר התך זה דניאל ולמה נקרא שמו התך שחתכוהו מגדולתו צריכין אנו לומר שזהו כורש הראשון שלפני אחשורוש ולדברי האומר שכל דברי מלכות נחתכין על פיו נאמר כורש זה הוא דריוש השני אחר אחשורוש ובימי דריוש המדי שהשליכו לגוב אריות לא ירד מגדולתו שנאמר (לקמן ו) ודניאל דנא הצלח במלכות דריוש ובמלכות כורש פרסאה למדנו שבימי כורש הראשון היה בגדולה:
rashi.eng: *And Daniel was there.* in greatness in Babylon until the first year of King Cyrus. According to the one who says that Hathach (Esther; 4:5, 6, 9, 10) is Daniel; and why was he called Hathach? Because he was cut off (חֲתָכוּהוּ) from his greatness; [according to his explanation] we must say that this is Cyrus I, who preceded Ahasuerus. But according to the one who says that all royal affairs were decided (נֶחְתָּכִים) by his orders, we must say that this Cyrus was Darius II, [who came] after Ahasuerus, and in the days of Darius the Mede, when they cast [Daniel] into the lions’ den, he was not demoted from his greatness, as it is said (6:29): “And this Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and during the reign of Cyrus the Persian.” We learn that during the days of Cyrus I he was [still] in his greatness.

notes.61: (tn, Heb): “Nebuchadnezzar’s.” The possessive pronoun is substituted in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.62: (tn, Heb): “dreamed dreams.” The plural is used here and in v. 2, but the singular in v. 3. The plural “dreams” has been variously explained. Some interpreters take the plural as denoting an indefinite singular (so GKC 400 �124.o). But it may be that it is describing a stream of related dreams, or a dream state. In the latter case, one might translate: “Nebuchadnezzar was in a trance.” See further, J. A. Montgomery, Daniel (ICC), 142.
notes.64: (tn, Heb): “his sleep left (?) him.” The use of the verb הָיָה (hayah, “to be”) here is unusual. The context suggests a meaning such as “to be finished” or “gone.” Cf. Dan 8:27. Some scholars emend the verb to read נָדְדָה (nad�dah, “fled”); cf. Dan 6:19. See further, DCH 2:540 s.v. היה I Ni.3; HALOT 244 s.v. היה nif; BDB 227-28 s.v. הָיָה Niph.2.

rashi.heb:
*ובשנת שתים למלכות נבוכדנצר.* 
אי אפשר לומר כן אלא בשנת שתים לחורבן הבית כך שנויה בסדר עולם וקראו למלכות נבוכדנצר על שהראה זדונו לכנס לתוך דביר מלכו של עולם:
rashi.eng: *Now in the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign.* It is impossible to say this, except that [it happened] in the second year after the destruction of the Temple. So it is taught in Seder Olam (ch. 28), and Scripture called it “of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign,” because he demonstrated his insolence by entering the Inner Sanctum of the Sovereign of the Universe.

rashi.heb:
*ותתפעם רוחו.* 
בפרעה נאמר ותפעם רוחו (בראשית מ״א:ח׳) שלא נעלם ממנו אלא פתרון החלום וכאן שנעלם ממנו גם החלום נכפלה הלשון ותתפעם לשון פעימה והלימה, ובחומש פירש"י ז"ל לשון נקיפה:
rashi.eng: *and his spirit was troubled.* Heb. וַתִּתְפָּעֶם רוּחוֹ. Concerning Pharaoh it says (Gen. 41:8): וַתִּפָּעֶם רוּחוֹ, for only the interpretation of the dream was hidden from him, but here, since the dream too was hidden from him, the expression is doubled: וַתִּתְפָּעֶם, an expression of pulsating and beating.

rashi.heb:
*נהיתה עליו.* 
לשון שברון כמו (יחזקאל ו) הווה על הווה:
rashi.eng: *was interrupted.* Heb. נִהְיְתָה, an expression of breaking like (Ezek. 7:25): “Breach upon breach (הוָה עַל הוָה).”

notes.66: (tn, Heb): “Chaldeans.” The term Chaldeans (Hebrew כַּשְׂדִּים, kasdim) is used in the book of Daniel both in an ethnic sense and, as here, to refer to a caste of Babylonian wise men and astrologers.
notes.67: (tn, Heb): “to explain to the king his dreams.”

notes.69: (tn, Heb): “I have dreamed a dream” (so KJV, ASV).

notes.71: (sn): Contrary to common belief, the point here is not that the wise men (Chaldeans) replied to the king in the Aramaic language, or that this language was uniquely the language of the Chaldeans. It was this view that led in the past to Aramaic being referred to as “Chaldee.” Aramaic was used as a lingua franca during this period; its origins and usage were not restricted to the Babylonians. Rather, this phrase is better understood as an editorial note (cf. NAB) marking the fact that from 2:4b through 7:28 the language of the book shifts from Hebrew to Aramaic. In 8:1, and for the remainder of the book, the language returns to Hebrew. Various views have been advanced to account for this change of language, most of which are unconvincing. Most likely the change in language is a reflection of stages in the transmission history of the book of Daniel.

rashi.heb:
*לעלמין חיי.* 
לעולם יחיה:
rashi.eng: *May the king live forever.* Aram. מַלְכָּא לְעָלְמִין חֱיִי.

rashi.heb:
*אמר חלמא לעבדך.* 
אמור החלום לעבדך:
rashi.eng: *Tell your servants the dream.* [as translated,] Tell your servants the dream.

notes.73: (tn): Aram “answered and said,” a common idiom to indicate a reply, but redundant in contemporary English.
notes.74: (tn): It seems clear from what follows that Nebuchadnezzar clearly recalls the content of the dream, although obviously he does not know what to make of it. By not divulging the dream itself to the would-be interpreters, he intends to find out whether they are simply leading him on. If they can tell him the dream’s content, which he is able to verify, he then can have confidence in their interpretation, which is what eludes him. The translation “the matter is gone from me” (cf. KJV, ASV), suggesting that the king had simply forgotten the dream, is incorrect. The Aramaic word used here (אַזְדָּא, ’azda’) is probably of Persian origin; it occurs in the OT only here and in v. 8. There are two main possibilities for the meaning of the word: “the matter is promulgated by me” (see KBL 1048 s.v.) and therefore “publicly known” (cf. NRSV; F. Rosenthal, Grammar, 62-63, �189), or “the matter is irrevocable” (cf. NAB, NIV, TEV, CEV, NLT; HALOT 1808 s.v. אזד; cf. also BDB 1079 s.v.). The present translation reflects this latter option. See further E. Vogt, Lexicon linguae aramaicae, 3.

rashi.heb:
*מילתה מני אזדא.* 
הדבר ממני הלך:
rashi.eng: *The matter has escaped me.* The thing has left me.

rashi.heb:
*הן לא תהודעונני חלמא ופשריה.* 
אם לא תודיעוני החלום ופתרונו:
rashi.eng: *If you do not let me know the dream and its meaning.* [as translated,] if you do not let me know the dream and its meaning.

rashi.heb:
*הדמין תתעבדון.* 
לאברים תתחתכו והרבה יש בגמרא הדומי הדמוה במסכת גיטין:
rashi.eng: *you shall be torn limb from limb.* Aram. הַדָמִין תִּתְעַבְּדוּן. You shall be cut to pieces, and there are many such in the Gemara (Gittin 67b): “Arrange the cuts” הַדְמּוּה) (ָהַדוּמֵי.

rashi.heb:
*נולי.* 
אשפה:
rashi.eng: *a dungheap.* Aram. נְוָלִי, a dungheap.

rashi.heb:
*יתשמון.* 
לשון וישם יהון שומות לאשפות:
rashi.eng: *shall be made.* Aram. יִתְּשָּׂמוּן an expression of וְיָשֵּׂם, and he will make. They shall be made into dungheaps.

rashi.heb:
*והן.* 
ואם:
rashi.eng: *But if.* [as translated,] But if.

rashi.heb:
*ונבזבה.* 
דורנות:
rashi.eng: *and lavish presents.* [as translated,] presents.

rashi.heb:
*להן.* 
אך:
rashi.eng: *but.* [as translated,] but.

rashi.heb:
*החוני.* 
תגידו לי:
rashi.eng: *tell me.* [as translated,] tell me.

rashi.heb:
*תנינות.* 
שנית:
rashi.eng: *a second time.* [as translated,] a second time.

rashi.heb:
*נהחוה.* 
נגיד:
rashi.eng: *we shall tell.* [as translated,] we shall tell.

rashi.heb:
*מן יציב ידע אנה.* 
באמת יודע אני:
rashi.eng: *in truth, I know.* [as translated,] in truth, I know.

rashi.heb:
*יציב.* 
דבר אמת ויציב:
rashi.eng: *truth.* Aram. יַצִיב, a true and permanent thing.

rashi.heb:
*די עדנא אנתון זבנין.* 
אשר זו השעה אתם מסורים למות:
rashi.eng: *that this time you are doomed.* Aram. אַנְתוּן זַבְנִין דִּי עִדָּנָא, that this time you are delivered to death.

rashi.heb:
*כל קבל די חזיתון.* 
כל כנגד שאתם רואים שהלך ממני הדבר ואתם כופלים לי להגיד לכם:
rashi.eng: *because you see.* because you see that the matter escaped me, but you repeatedly ask me to tell you.

notes.78: (tn): Aram “one is your law,” i.e., only one thing is applicable to you.

rashi.heb:
*די הן חלמא לא תהודעינני.* 
שאם החלום ופתרונו לא תודיעוני אחת היא דתכם למות:
rashi.eng: *For if you do not tell me the dream.* [This means]: If you do not tell me the dream and its interpretation, you have, but one sentence and that is death.

rashi.heb:
*ומלה כדבה ושחיתה הזדמנתון.* 
או אם דבר כזב ונשחת תכינו עצמכם לומר לפני:
rashi.eng: *or if you have prepared yourselves… a false and corrupt word.* Or if you have prepared yourselves to say before me a false and corrupt word.

rashi.heb:
*עד די עדנא ישתנא.* 
עד אשר ישתנה העת כלומר קודם נטות צללי ערב שישתנה מועד הבוקר:
rashi.eng: *until the time changes.* until the time changes, i.e., before the shadows of evening slant, when the time of morning changes.

rashi.heb:
*עד די עדנא ישתנא.* 
ל' גערה וגזום הוא כך יענש והעונש כבר פירש למעלה ודוגמתו לכן כל הורג קין (בראשית ד׳:ט״ו):
rashi.eng: *until the time changes.*  “Until the time changes” is an expression of rebuke and an exaggeration: so will he be punished, and the punishment was already delineated above. A similar instance is (Gen. 4:15): “Therefore, whoever kills Cain.”

rashi.heb:
*להן.* 
אך החלום אמרו לי מה חלמתי, ואדע כ"ש שהפתרון תגידו:
rashi.eng: *but.* the dream; tell me what I dreamed, and I shall know that you will surely tell me the interpretation.

rashi.heb:
*די מלת מלכא.* 
אשר דבר המלך יוכל להגיד:
rashi.eng: *who… the king’s word.* who will be able to tell the king’s word.

rashi.heb:
*כל קבל.* 
כל כנגד כלומר תשובתינו זו אמת היא לעומת שלא היה מלך מעולם ששאל דבר כזה:
rashi.eng: *because.* Aram. כָּל קַבֵל, lit. all opposite; i.e., our reply is true, in view of the fact that there was never a king who asked anything like this.

rashi.heb:
*מלה כדנה.* 
דבר כזה:
rashi.eng: *such a thing.* Aram. מִלָה כִדְּנָה, a thing like this.

rashi.heb:
*ואשף.* 
הדוחק במזל:
rashi.eng: *astrologer.* who presses the constellation.

notes.82: (tn): Aram “whose dwelling is not with flesh.”

rashi.heb:
*יקירה.* 
כבדה ומשאה כבד:
rashi.eng: *difficult.* Aram. יַקִירָה, heavy, and its burden is heavy.

rashi.heb:
*ואחרן לא איתי די יחוינה.* 
ואחר אין אשר יגידה:
rashi.eng: *and there is no other who can tell it.* and there is no other who will tell it.

rashi.heb:
*להן אלהין.* 
אך המלאכים אשר מדורם עם בשר ודם איננו:
rashi.eng: *but the angels.* but the angels whose dwelling is not with flesh and blood.

rashi.heb:
*מדריהון.* 
מגוריהון ומדרש רבי תנחומא ואחרן לא איתי. ואהרן לא איתי כהן הלובש אורים ותומים אינו כאן שיגיד לך אמר להם כל כך היה כח באותו בית ונתתם לי עצה להחריבו מיד כעס וצוה להרגן:
rashi.eng: *whose dwelling.* Aram. מְדָרְהוֹן, their dwelling. The Midrash of Rabbi Tanhuma (ad loc.) [says]: וְאַחֲרָן לָא אִיתַי, and Aaron is not here. A priest who wears the Urim and Tummim is not here to tell you. He said to them, “That Temple was so powerful, and you advised me to destroy it?” Immediately, he became angry and commanded to slay them.

notes.83: (tn): Aram “was angry and very furious.” The expression is a hendiadys (two words or phrases expressing a single idea).

rashi.heb:
*כל קבל דנה.* 
לעומת התשובה הזאת:
rashi.eng: *In view of this.* in view of this reply.

rashi.heb:
*מלכא בנס וקצף שגיא.* 
היה המלך בזעף וקצף גדול:
rashi.eng: *in great wrath and anger.* Aram. מַלְכָּא בְּנַס וּקְצַף שַּׂגִיא. The king was in great wrath and anger.

rashi.heb:
*בנס.* 
בזעף, והנם זועפים (בראשית מ׳:ו׳) ת"א והא אינון נסיסין:
rashi.eng: *in great wrath.* (בְּנַס) means in wrath. (Gen. 40:6): "And behold they were angry (זֹעַפִים), and Onkelos renders: נסִיסִין.

rashi.heb:
*ואמר להובדה.* 
ויאמר להאביד, וי"ו של ואמר נתעצמו בו מנחם ודונ"ש, מנחם דחק עצמו לתת ב' של בנס ביסוד התיבה ולא פתר בנס וקצף לשון שמות דברים אלא לשון פעל רגז וקצף הרבה ואמר להאביד וי"ו שבואמר דחקו לפתור כן ודונש אמר אי אפשר להיות ב' בנס יסוד בתיבה אלא שם דבר הוא וכן פתרו בזעף וקצף גדול אמר להאביד ושם הוי"ו טפילה ויתירה כמו וי"ו של ורכב וסוס (תהילים ע״ו:ז׳), ואני אומר אין הוי"ו דחוקה להיות טפילה ויתירה כי כן פתרונו מלכא בנס וקצף שגיא המלך נהיה בזעף וקצף גדול ואמר בזעפו להאבידם ומן המקראות קצרי לשון היא:
rashi.eng: *and ordered to destroy.* Aram. וַאֲמַר לְהוֹבָדָה. About this “vav” of וַאֲמַר, Menahem and Dunash disputed. Menahem (p. 46) forced himself to make the “beth” of בְּנַס, a radical and did not interpret בְּנַס וּקְצַף as nouns, but as an expression of a verb: was greatly wroth and angry and ordered to destroy. The “vav” in וַאֲמַר forced him to interpret it this way. Dunash (p. 9) says that it is impossible for the “beth” to be a radical, but it is a noun, and he interpreted it in this manner: with great wrath and anger he ordered to destroy, and the “vav” there is superfluous, like the “vav” of (Ps. 76:7): “chariot (וְרֶכֶב) and horse.” But I say that the “vav” is not forced to be superfluous, but so is its interpretation: מַלְכָּא בְּנַס וּקְצַף שַּׂגִּיא, the king was in great wrath and anger, and he ordered in his wrath to destroy them. Accordingly, this is an elliptical verse.

notes.84: (tn): The Aramaic participle is used here to express the imminent future.
notes.85: (tn): The impersonal active plural (“they sought”) of the Aramaic verb could also be translated as an English passive: “Daniel and his friends were sought” (cf. NAB).

rashi.heb:
*ודתא נפקת.* 
דת המלך וגזירתו יצא במדינה:
rashi.eng: *And a decree was issued.* The law of the king and his decree were issued in the province.

rashi.heb:
*ובעו דניאל וחברוהי להתקטלה.* 
ונתבקשו דניאל וחביריו ליהרג:
rashi.eng: *and Daniel and his colleagues were sought to be slain.* [as translated,] and Daniel and his colleagues were sought to be slain.

notes.86: (tn): Aram “returned prudence and counsel.” The expression is a hendiadys.

rashi.heb:
*באדין.* 
תרגום של אז:
rashi.eng: *Then.* Aram. בֵּאדַיִן, the Targum for אָז.

rashi.heb:
*התיב עטא וטעם לאריוך.* 
השיב עצה וטעם לאריוך שם האיש:
rashi.eng: *answered with counsel and good sense.* He answered [with] counsel and good sense to Arioch, the name of the man.

rashi.heb:
*רב טבחיא.* 
שר ההורגים המחוייבים הריגה:
rashi.eng: *the… chief executioner.* the officer over those who executed the ones condemned to death.

notes.87: (tn): The Aramaic word מְהַחְצְפָה (m�hakhts�fah) may refer to the severity of the king’s decree (i.e., “harsh”; so HALOT 1879 s.v. חצף; BDB 1093 s.v. חֲצַף), although it would seem that in a delicate situation such as this Daniel would avoid this kind of criticism of the king’s actions. The translation above understands the word to refer to the immediacy, not harshness, of the decree. See further, F. Rosenthal, Grammar, 50, �116; E. Vogt, Lexicon linguae aramaicae, 67.

rashi.heb:
*על מה דתא מהחצפה.* 
מה זה שדת המלך חצופה להרוג:
rashi.eng: *Why was the decree issued so hastily.* Why is the decree of the king [issued] in such a haste to kill?

rashi.heb:
*אדין מלתא הודע אריוך לדניאל.* 
שקצף המלך על שאין מגיד חלומו:
rashi.eng: *Then Arioch made the matter known to Daniel.* that the king was angry because no one told him his dream.

notes.88: (tc): Theodotion and the Syriac lack the words “went in and.”

rashi.heb:
*על ובעא.* 
נכנס ובקש:
rashi.eng: *entered and requested.* [as translated,] entered and requested.

rashi.heb:
*ינתן ליה.* 
יתן לו:
rashi.eng: *be given him.* [as translated,] be given him.

notes.89: (tn): Aram “Daniel.” The proper name is redundant here in English, and has not been included in the translation.

rashi.heb:
*רזא גלי.* 
בסתר נגלה:
rashi.eng: *the secret was revealed.* [as translated,] the secret was revealed.

notes.92: (sn): As is often the case in the Bible, here the name represents the person.

rashi.heb:
*מהשנא.* 
מחליף:
rashi.eng: *changes.* [as translated,] changes.

rashi.heb:
*מהעדה.* 
מסיר מלכין על שהבין מתוך החלום שמלכות נבוכדנצר פוסקת ומלכות אחרת עומדת:
rashi.eng: *removes.* He removes kings, for he understood from the dream that Nebuchadnezzar’s kingdom would terminate, and another kingdom would rise.

rashi.heb:
*הוא גלא עמיקתא.* 
גולה עמוקות:
rashi.eng: *He reveals the profound.* [as translated,] He reveals the profound.

rashi.heb:
*ומסתרתא.* 
על שגלה לו עומק זה:
rashi.eng: *and secret things.* for He revealed this profound thing to me.

notes.96: (tn): Aram “we.” Various explanations have been offered for the plural, but it is probably best understood as the editorial plural; so also with “me” later in this verse.

rashi.heb:
*הודעתנא.* 
הודעתני:
rashi.eng: *You have let me know.* [as translated,] You have let me know.

notes.98: (tc): The MT has עַל עַל (’al ’al, “he entered upon”). Several medieval Hebrew MSS lack the verb, although this may be due to haplography.
notes.99: (tc): The LXX and Vulgate, along with one medieval Hebrew MS, lack this verb.
notes.100: (tn): Aram “cause me to enter.” So also in v. 25.

rashi.heb:
*כל קבל דנה.* 
כל עומת זה שנגלה לו הסוד:
rashi.eng: *In view of this.* in view of this, that the secret was revealed to him.

rashi.heb:
*דניאל על על אריוך.* 
נכנס אצל אריוך:
rashi.eng: *Daniel came in to Arioch.* He entered Arioch’s premises.

rashi.heb:
*די מני.* 
שהפקיד:
rashi.eng: *had appointed.* [as translated,] had appointed.

rashi.heb:
*אל תהובד.* 
אל תאבד:
rashi.eng: *Do not destroy.* [as translated,] Do not destroy.

rashi.heb:
*העלני.* 
הכניסני:
rashi.eng: *bring me in.* [as translated,] bring me in.

notes.102: (sn): Arioch’s claim is self-serving and exaggerated. It is Daniel who came to him, and not the other way around. By claiming to have found one capable of solving the king’s dilemma, Arioch probably hoped to ingratiate himself to the king.

rashi.heb:
*אדין.* 
אז:
rashi.eng: *Then.* Aram. אֶדַיִן, [the equivalent of] אָז.

rashi.heb:
*בהתבהלה.* 
בבהלה כלומר במהירות:
rashi.eng: *in haste.* Aram. בְּהִתְבְּהָלָה, in haste, i. e., quickly.

rashi.heb:
*הנעל.* 
הכניס את דניאל:
rashi.eng: *brought… in.* brought Daniel in.

rashi.heb:
*די השכחת גבר.* 
אשר מצאתי איש:
rashi.eng: *that “I have found a man.* [as translated,] that” I have found a man.

rashi.heb:
*גלותא די יהוד.* 
גלות יהודה:
rashi.eng: *the exiles of Judea.* [as translated,] the exiles of Judea.

rashi.heb:
*האיתך כהל.* 
הישך יכול:
rashi.eng: *Do you have the ability.* Are you able?

rashi.heb:
*די חזית.* 
אשר ראיתי:
rashi.eng: *that I have seen.* [as translated,] that I have seen.

rashi.heb:
*גזרין.* 
שם מין בעל כישוף:
rashi.eng: *demonologists.* Aram. גָזְרִין, the name of a type of ruler over demons.

notes.103: (tn): Aram “a revealer of mysteries.” The phrase serves as a quasi-title for God in Daniel.
notes.105: (tn): Aram “your dream and the visions of your head upon your bed.”

rashi.heb:
*ברם איתי וגו': והודע למלכא וגו'.* 
הוא גילה לי רז זה ועל ידו הודיע למלך עיקר חלומו בעתידות:
rashi.eng: *But there is… and He lets Nebuchadnezzar know.* He revealed this secret to me, and through me let the king know that his dream refers to future events.

rashi.heb:
*חלמך וחזוי ראשך על משכבך.* 
אשר על משכבך זהו:
rashi.eng: *your dream and the visions of your head on your bed.* which are on your bed.

notes.106: (tn): Aram “your thoughts upon your bed went up to what will be after this.”

rashi.heb:
*רעיונך.* 
הרהורך:
rashi.eng: *your thoughts.* Aram. רַעְיוֹנָיךְ.

rashi.heb:
*על משכבך סליקו.* 
מה שהיית מהרהר ביום מה יהיה אחריך על משכבך עלו:
rashi.eng: *came while on your bed.* What you were thinking of during the day, what would be after you, came [to you] on your bed.

rashi.heb:
*וגלא רזיא הודעך.* 
והקב"ה מגלה רזים הודיעך את אשר יהיה:
rashi.eng: *and the Revealer of secrets.* and the Holy One, blessed be He, Who reveals secrets, let you know what will come about.

notes.107: (tn): Aram “not for any wisdom which is in me more than [in] any living man.”
notes.108: (tn): Aram “they might cause the king to know.” The impersonal plural is used here to refer to the role of God’s spirit in revealing the dream and its interpretation to the king. As J. A. Montgomery says, “it appropriately here veils the mysterious agency” (Daniel [ICC], 164-65).

rashi.heb:
*ואנה לא בחכמה.* 
ואני לא מרוב החכמה שיש בי משאר הבריות יותר נגלה לי הסוד הזה:
rashi.eng: *And I, not with wisdom.* And I, not with superior wisdom that I have, more than other creatures, was this secret revealed to me.

rashi.heb:
*להן על דברת די פשרא למלכא יהודעון.* 
יודיעוך מן השמים:
rashi.eng: *but in order that they should let the king know the interpretation.* They should let you know from heaven.

rashi.heb:
*ורעיוני לבבך תנדע.* 
והרהורי לבבך שאתה מהרהר תמיד לדעת מי יקום אחריך:
rashi.eng: *and you should know the thoughts of your heart.* and the thoughts of your heart about which you are constantly thinking, [which are] to know who will rise after you.

rashi.heb:
*תנדע.* 
תדע:
rashi.eng: *you should know.* [as translated,] you should know.

rashi.heb:
*חזה הוית.* 
רואה היית:
rashi.eng: *you were watching.* [as translated,] you were watching.

rashi.heb:
*ואלו.* 
לשון והנה:
rashi.eng: *and behold.* Aram. וַאֲלוּ, an expression of “behold.”

rashi.heb:
*צלמא דכן רב.* 
צלם אשר היה לו כן גדול:
rashi.eng: *an image which had a large base.* [as translated,] an image which had a large base.

rashi.heb:
*וזיוה יתיר קאם לקבלך.* 
היה עומד לנגדך:
rashi.eng: *with unusual splendor, was standing opposite you.* [as translated,] standing opposite you.

rashi.heb:
*ורוה דחיל.* 
ותארו נורא:
rashi.eng: *and its form was frightening.* [as translated,] and its form was frightening.

rashi.heb:
*די דהב טב.* 
של זהב טוב:
rashi.eng: *of fine gold.* [as translated,] of fine gold.

rashi.heb:
*חדוהי.* 
חזה שלו:
rashi.eng: *its breast.* [as translated,] its breast.

rashi.heb:
*ודרעוהי.* 
וזרועותיו:
rashi.eng: *and its arms.* [as translated,] and its arms.

rashi.heb:
*מעוהי וירכתיה.* 
בטנו וירכותיו:
rashi.eng: *its belly and thighs.* [as translated,] its belly and thighs.

notes.111: (sn): Clay refers to baked clay, which – though hard – was also fragile. Cf. the reference in v. 41 to “wet clay.”

rashi.heb:
*שקוהי די פרזל.* 
שוקיו של ברזל: מנהן די פרזל:
rashi.eng: *Its legs were of iron.* [as translated,] Its legs were of iron.

rashi.heb:
*ומנהן די חסף.* 
מהם של ברזל ומהם של חרס:
rashi.eng: *were partly of iron and partly of clay.* [as translated,] were partly of iron and partly of clay [i.e., part of each foot was of iron and part of clay].

notes.113: (tc): The LXX, Theodotion, and the Vulgate have “from a mountain,” though this is probably a harmonization with v. 45.

rashi.heb:
*די התגזרת אבן.* 
אשר נחתכה ונבדלה אבן אחת:
rashi.eng: *until one stone was hewn.* that one stone was cut and separated.

rashi.heb:
*די לא בידין.* 
אשר לא בידים כי אם מאיליה:
rashi.eng: *without hands.* not with hands, but by itself.

rashi.heb:
*ומחת לצלמא.* 
והכת' את הצלם:
rashi.eng: *and it struck the image.* [as translated,] and it struck the image.

rashi.heb:
*והדקת המון.* 
והדיקה אותם:
rashi.eng: *and crumbled them.* [as translated,] and crumbled them.

notes.114: (tn): Aram “as one.” For the meaning “without distinction” see the following: F. Rosenthal, Grammar, 36, �64, and p. 93; E. Vogt, Lexicon linguae aramaicae, 60.

rashi.heb:
*באדין דקו כחדה.* 
אז הודקו יחד כל מיני מתכות וחרס שהיה בו:
rashi.eng: *Then… crumbled together.* Then all the types of metals and the clay that were in it crumbled together.

rashi.heb:
*והוו כעור מן אידרי קיט.* 
והיו כמוץ מגרנות הקיץ:
rashi.eng: *and they were like chaff from the threshing floors of the summer.* [as translated,] and they were like chaff from the threshing floors of the summer.

rashi.heb:
*ונשא המון רוחא.* 
ותשא אותם הרוח:
rashi.eng: *and the wind carried them off.* [as translated,] and the wind carried them off.

rashi.heb:
*וכל אתר לא השתכח להון.* 
כלומר לא נודע מקומה הראשון ולא ניכר שהיו שם מעולם:
rashi.eng: *and no place was found for them.* i.e., their original place was unknown, and it was unrecognizable that they were ever there.

rashi.heb:
*הות לטור רב.* 
נעשית הר גדול:
rashi.eng: *became a huge mountain.* [as translated,] became a huge mountain.

notes.115: (tn): Various suggestions have been made concerning the plural “we.” It is probably the editorial plural and could be translated here as “I.”

rashi.heb:
*דנה חלמא.* 
הרי זה החלום שחלמת:
rashi.eng: *This is the dream.* Behold this is the dream that you dreamed.

rashi.heb:
*ופשריה נאמר וגו'.* 
ופתרונו נאמר לך:
rashi.eng: *and its interpretation we shall recite, etc..* and its interpretation we shall tell you.

rashi.heb:
*מלך מלכיא.* 
פירשו רז"ל כל מלך מלכיא דדניאל מלך ב"ו חוץ מזה שכנגד הקב"ה אמר וכן פתרונו מלך המלכי' שהוא אלקי השמי':
rashi.eng: *The King of kings.* Our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Shev. 35b): Every mention of “king” in Daniel refers to an earthly king, except this one, which he said in reference to the Holy One, blessed be He, and this is what it means: The King of kings, Who is the God of heaven.

rashi.heb:
*מלכותא חסנא.* 
מלכות חזק וכבד נתן לך:
rashi.eng: *a strong… kingdom.* gave you a strong and prominent kingdom.

rashi.heb:
*והשלטך בכלהון.* 
והשליטך על כולם שאפילו גוזר על הסוס לא יהא צונף ועל העוף לא יפרח כמו שנאמר ואת חית השדה נתתי לעבדו (ירמיה כז):
rashi.eng: *and has given you dominion over them all.* And He gave you dominion over them all, so that even if you decree upon a horse, it will not whinny, or upon a bird, it will not fly, as it is said (Jer. 27:6): “and even the beasts of the field I have given to him to serve him.”

rashi.heb:
*אנת הוא ראשה די דהבא.* 
ראש הזהב של הצורה שראית אתה הוא שמלכותך חזקה ועתה קיימת והיא חשובה מאד:
rashi.eng: *You are the head of gold.* You are the golden head of the image that you saw, for your kingdom is strong, and now it is in existence and is very prominent.

notes.119: (sn): The identity of the first kingdom is clearly Babylon. The identification of the following three kingdoms is disputed. The common view is that they represent Media, Persia, and Greece. Most conservative scholars identify them as Media-Persia, Greece, and Rome.

rashi.heb:
*ובתרך תקום מלכו אחרי: ארע מנך.* 
ואחריך אחר מלכות בלשצר בנך תקום מלכות שתטול השררה מזרעך נמוכה ושפלה ממלכות שלך:
rashi.eng: *And after you will arise another kingdom lower than you.* And after you, after the reign of your son, Belshazzar, will arise a kingdom that will take the ruling power from your seed, lower and humbler than your kingdom.

rashi.heb:
*ארע.* 
תחתונה ונמוכה, כמו שהכסף נמוך ושפל מהזהב, וראית שהחזה שהיא אחר הראש היא של כסף כך תהא מלכות מדי ופרס אחר מלכות בבל שפלה ממלכות נבוכדנצר:
rashi.eng: *lower.* Aram. אֶרַע, lower, as silver is lower and humbler than gold, and you saw that the breast, which is after the head, was of silver; so will the kingdom of Media and Persia, which will follow the kingdom of Babylon, be humbler than the kingdom of Nebuchadnezzar.

rashi.heb:
*ומלכו תליתאה אחרי.* 
אחרת:
rashi.eng: *and another, a third kingdom.* [as translated,] another.

rashi.heb:
*די נחשא.* 
חסינא כנחשת והיא מלכות יון מלכות אלכסנדרוס מוקדן:
rashi.eng: *of copper.* as strong as copper, and that is the kingdom of Alexander of Macedon.

notes.120: (tc): Theodotion and the Vulgate lack the phrase “and as iron breaks in pieces.”
notes.121: (tn): The Aramaic text does not have this word, but it has been added in the translation for clarity.
notes.122: (tn): The words “the others” are supplied from the context.

rashi.heb:
*ומלכו.* 
רביעאה היא קשה כפרזלא כאשר ראית השוקיים שהם רביעים לראש ולחזה ולמעיים והם של ברזל:
rashi.eng: *And a fourth kingdom.* will be as hard as iron, as you saw the thighs, which are the fourth from the head, the breast, and the belly, and they are of iron.

rashi.heb:
*מהדק וחשל כלא.* 
מרדד ומהדק כל מיני מתכות שמרדדין אותם בקורנס:
rashi.eng: *crumbles and flattens everything.* flattens and crumbles all kinds of metal, which are flattened with a hammer.

rashi.heb:
*וחשל.* 
ומרדד והרבה יש בגמ' חשלי דודי (כתובות עז) ביעי חשילתא (חולין צב):
rashi.eng: *and flattens.* Aram. וְחָשֵּׁל, and flattens. There are many such [words] in the Talmud. Keth. 77a, “who thins copper for kettles (חַשְּׁלָא דוּדֵי);” Hul. 93a: “crushed testicles (בֵּיעֵי חֳשִּׁלָתָא).”

rashi.heb:
*כל אלין.* 
כל מיני מתכות הללו שראית בצלם:
rashi.eng: *all these.* all these kinds of metals that you saw in the image.

rashi.heb:
*תדיק ותרוע.* 
תדיק ותרוצץ:
rashi.eng: *it will crumble and shatter.* It will crumble and shatter all the nations.

rashi.heb:
*חסף די פחר.* 
חרס של יוצר והרבה יש בגמרא מאני דפחרא:
rashi.eng: *potter’s clay.* Aram. חֲסַף דִּי פֶחָר, a potter’s clay, and there are many instances of this in the Talmud (Taanith 7a): “vessels of a potter (מָאנֵי דְפַחְרָא).”

rashi.heb:
*מלכו פליגה תהוה.* 
מלכות חלוקה תהיה שני מלכים יהיו ממנה כאחד חזק וחלש כמו שמפורש למטה מן קצת מלכותא תהוה תקיפא:
rashi.eng: *it will be a divided kingdom.* It will be a divided kingdom; two kings will rise from it at once, strong and weak, as explained below (verse 42): “part of the kingdom will be strong.”

rashi.heb:
*ומן נצבתא די פרזלא להוא בה.* 
אף החלש יהא חזק על אחרים ע"י חוזק חברו שיראו מפניו וזה מן נצבתא די פרזלא להוי בה, מן חוזק מצב הברזל, יהיה במלך החלש:
rashi.eng: *and in it will be some of the strength of iron.* Even the weak one will be stronger than the other nations through the strength of his fellow, for they will fear him. And this is the meaning of וּמִן נִצְבְּתָא דִּי פַרְזְלָא לֶהֶוֵא בָהּ; some of the strength of the stability of iron will be in the weak king.

rashi.heb:
*כל קבל די חזיתה.* 
כל עומת שראית ברזל מעורב בחרסית הטיט:
rashi.eng: *in view of what you saw.* in view of what you saw-iron mixed with clay.

notes.126: (tc): The present translation reads the conjunction, with most medieval Hebrew MSS, LXX, Vulgate, and the Qere. The Kethib lacks the conjunction.
notes.127: (sn): The reference to people being mixed is usually understood to refer to intermarriage.
notes.129: (tc): The present translation reads הֵיךְ דִּי (hekh diy) rather than the MT הֵא־כְדִי (he’-kh�di). It is a case of wrong word division.

rashi.heb:
*מתערבין להון בזרע אנשא וגו'.* 
מתחתנים יהיו עם שאר האומות ולא יהיו שלימים ונדבקים עמם באמת ולב שלם ודתיהם שונות מדתי שאר האומות:
rashi.eng: *that they will mingle with the seed of men.* They will intermarry with the other nations but they will not be at peace and truly cleave to them wholeheartedly, and their laws will differ from the laws of the other nations.

rashi.heb:
*הא כדי פרזלא לא מתערב.* 
הלא הוא כמו שאין הברזל נדבק יפה עם החרס:
rashi.eng: *as iron does not mix with clay.* Is it not just as iron does not stick well to clay?

rashi.heb:
*וביומיהון די מלכיא אנון.* 
ביומיהון של מלכים הללו בעוד מלכותם של רומיים קיימת:
rashi.eng: *And in the days of these kings.* in the days of these kings, when the kingdom of Rome is still in existence.

rashi.heb:
*יקים אלה שמיא.* 
מלכות הקב"ה שלעולם לא תתחבל מלכו והיא מלכות מלך המשיח:
rashi.eng: *the God Of heaven will set up a kingdom.* The kingdom of the Holy One, blessed be He, which will never be destroyed, is the kingdom of the Messiah.

rashi.heb:
*תדק ותסף.* 
תדק ותכלה כל אלו המלכיות:
rashi.eng: *it will crumble and destroy.* It will crumble and destroy all these kingdoms.

rashi.heb:
*כל קבל די חזית.* 
כל עומת שראית שנתפרקה אבן מן ההר שהדיקה כל הצלם זה פתרון שהמלכות החמישית תכלה ותרוצץ את כולם:
rashi.eng: *Just as you saw.* just as you saw that a stone was broken off the mountain, which crumbled the entire image. This is the interpretation that the fifth kingdom will destroy and shatter them all.

rashi.heb:
*מה די להוא אחרי דנה.* 
מה שיהיה אחר זאת אחר מלכות זו שלך:
rashi.eng: *what will be after this.* what will be after this, after this kingdom of yours.

rashi.heb:
*ויציב חלמא.* 
אמת הוא החלום:
rashi.eng: *and its interpretation is reliable.* for the Eternal of Israel neither lies nor repents.

rashi.heb:
*אמר לנסכה.* 
רצה לעשותו אלוה:
rashi.eng: *ordered to offer up… libations.* He wished to deify him.

rashi.heb:
*מן קשוט.* 
באמת:
rashi.eng: *truly.* [as translated,] in truth.

rashi.heb:
*ומרא מלכין.* 
אדוני האדונים:
rashi.eng: *and the Master of the kings.* The Lord of lords.

rashi.heb:
*רזא דנה.* 
סתר זה:
rashi.eng: *this secret.* [as translated,] this secret.

rashi.heb:
*לדניאל רבי.* 
לדניאל גדל על כל השרים:
rashi.eng: *elevated Daniel.* He elevated Daniel over all the princes.

notes.132: (tn): Aram “and Daniel sought from the king and he appointed.”
notes.133: (tn): Aram “was at the gate of the king.”

rashi.heb:
*ומני על עבידתא די מדינת בבל.* 
ויפקד על כל צרכי הממלכות את חנניה מישאל ועזריה:
rashi.eng: *and he appointed, over the affairs of the capital cities of Babylon.* He appointed, over all the necessities of the kingdom, Hananiah Mishael, and Azariah.

notes.134: (sn): The LXX introduces this chapter with the following chronological note: “in the eighteenth year of.” Such a date would place these events at about the time of the destruction of Jerusalem in 586 B.C. (cf. 2 Kgs 25:8). However, there seems to be no real basis for associating the events of Daniel 3 with this date.
notes.135: (sn): There is no need to think of Nebuchadnezzar’s image as being solid gold. No doubt the sense is that it was overlaid with gold (cf. Isa 40:19; Jer 10:3-4), with the result that it presented a dazzling self-compliment to the greatness of Nebuchadnezzar’s achievements.
notes.136: (sn): According to a number of patristic authors, the image represented a deification of Nebuchadnezzar himself. This is not clear from the biblical text, however.
notes.137: (tn): Aram “sixty cubits.” Assuming a length of 18 inches for the standard cubit, the image would be 90 feet (27.4 m) high.
notes.138: (tn): Aram “six cubits.” Assuming a length of 18 inches for the standard cubit, the image would be 9 feet (2.74 m) wide. The dimensions of the image (ninety feet high and nine feet wide) imply that it did not possess normal human proportions, unless a base for the image is included in the height dimension. The ancient world knew of other tall statues. For example, the Colossus of Rhodes – the huge statue of Helios which stood (ca. 280-224 B.C.) at the entrance to the harbor at Rhodes and was one of the seven wonders of the ancient world – was said to be seventy cubits (105 ft or 32 m) in height, which would make it even taller than Nebuchadnezzar’s image.

rashi.heb:
*עבד וגו'.* 
מלאה לבו לעשות צלם של זהב:
rashi.eng: *made an image.* He had an urge to make an image of gold.

rashi.heb:
*פתיה אמין שית אקימה וגו'.* 
אם אין עביו אלא שש היאך יכול לעמוד בגובה אמין שתין אמר רב ביבי מעמידין אותו ונופל עד שהביאו כל זהב של ירושלים ושפכו דימוס על רגליו לקיים מה שנאמ' (יחזקאל ז) וזהבם לנידה יהיה:
rashi.eng: *its width six cubits; he set it up etc..* If its thickness was only six [cubits], how could it stand at a height of sixty cubits? Said Rav Bibi: They would set it up and it would fall, until they brought all the gold of Jerusalem and poured a base around its feet, to fulfill what was said (Ezek. 7:19): “and their gold will be for a repugnant thing.”

rashi.heb:
*בבקעת דורא.* 
שם מקום:
rashi.eng: *in the plain of Dura.* the name of a place.

notes.139: (sn): The specific duties of the seven types of officials listed here (cf. vv. 3, 27) are unclear. The Aramaic words that are used are transliterations of Akkadian or Persian technical terms whose exact meanings are uncertain. The translations given here follow suggestions set forth in BDB.
notes.140: (tn): Aram “Nebuchadnezzar the king.” The proper name and title have been replaced by the relative pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*לאחשדרפניא.* 
דוכסין:
rashi.eng: *the satraps.* Aram. לַאֲחַשְּׁדַרְפְּנַיָּא dukes.

rashi.heb:
*פחותא.* 
שלטונין:
rashi.eng: *governors.* rulers.

rashi.heb:
*אדרגזריא גדבריא וגו'.* 
כולם שם עכו"ם הם:
rashi.eng: *the judges, the treasurers, etc..* They are all names of nations.

rashi.heb:
*לחנוכת צלמא.* 
תחלת עבודותיו:
rashi.eng: *the dedication of the image.* the beginning of its worship.

notes.141: (tc): The LXX and Theodotion lack the words “that Nebuchadnezzar had erected.”

notes.142: (tn): According to BDB 1097 s.v. כָּרוֹז the Aramaic word used here is a Greek loanword, but other scholars have argued instead for a Persian derivation (HALOT 1902 s.v. *כָּרוֹז).

rashi.heb:
*וכרוזא קרא בחיל.* 
הכרוז יוצא בכח גדול:
rashi.eng: *And the announcement was issued aloud.* [as translated,] and the announcement was issued aloud.

rashi.heb:
*לכון אמרין עממיא.* 
לכם כל העמים והלשונות אומרים מכרוז מצות המלך במשלחת המלך:
rashi.eng: *To you we are saying, O peoples.* [as translated,] To you, all peoples and nations, we are announcing the command of the king as a message from the king.

notes.145: (sn): The word zither (Aramaic קִיתָרוֹס [qitaros]), and the words for harp (Aramaic פְּסַנְתֵּרִין [p�santerin]) and pipes (Aramaic סוּמְפֹּנְיָה [sumpon�yah]), are of Greek derivation. Though much has been made of this in terms of suggesting a date in the Hellenistic period for the writing of the book, it is not surprising that a few Greek cultural terms, all of them the names of musical instruments, should appear in this book. As a number of scholars have pointed out, the bigger surprise (if, in fact, the book is to be dated to the Hellenistic period) may be that there are so few Greek loanwords in Daniel.
notes.146: (tn): The imperfect Aramaic verbs have here an injunctive nuance.

rashi.heb:
*בעדנא דתשמעון קל קרנא משרוקיתא.* 
קול הקרן שורקת כמו (זכריה י׳:ח׳) אשרקה להם ואקבצם:
rashi.eng: *At the time you hear the sound of the whistling horn.* Aram. קָל קַרְנָא מַשְּׁרוֹקֵיתָא, the sound of the whistling horn, like (Zech. 10:8) “I will whistle (אֶשְּׁרְקָא) to them, and I will gather them.”

rashi.heb:
*קתרוס סבכא וגו'.* 
כולם כלי זמר הם:
rashi.eng: *the clavichord, the harp, etc..* They are all musical instruments.

rashi.heb:
*זני זמרא.* 
מיני זמר למינו ת"א לזנוהי:
rashi.eng: *kinds of music.* Aram. זְנֵי זְמָרָא kinds of music. (Gen. 1:11) “After its kind,” Onkelos renders: לִזְנוֹהִי.

rashi.heb:
*אתון נורא.* 
גומא שעושין לשרוף בה אבנים לסיד והוא כבשן שבכל המקרא:
rashi.eng: *a fiery furnace.* a pit that is made to burn rocks into lime, and that is כִּבְשָּׁן in all the Scriptures.

notes.149: (tc): Though not in the Aramaic text of BHS, this word appears in many medieval Hebrew MSS, some LXX MSS, and Vulgate. Cf. vv. 5, 10, 15.

rashi.heb:
*כל קבל דנה.* 
כל עומת זו שנזהרו במצות המלך על כך:
rashi.eng: *In view of this.* in view of this, that they took heed to observe the king’s command concerning this. bagpipes would be played.

rashi.heb:
*בה זמנא.* 
בו בזמן שישמעו קול הזמר שהוא לסימן שיבואו המשתחוים להשתחוות נפלין כל עממיא וגו':
rashi.eng: *at that time.* At the time that they hear the sound of the music, which is a sign that those who prostrate themselves should come to prostrate, all peoples would fall etc.

notes.150: (tc): This expression is absent in Theodotion.
notes.152: (tn): Aram “ate the pieces of.” This is a rather vivid idiom for slander.

rashi.heb:
*כל קבל דנה.* 
כל עומת זו שראו שונאי היהודי' שיש שעה להלשין עליהם:
rashi.eng: *In view of this.* in view of this, that their enemies saw that there is a time to denounce them.

rashi.heb:
*קריבו גוברין כשדאין ואכלו קרצהון.* 
הלשינו עליהם, לא תלך רכיל (ויקרא י״ט:ט״ז) מתרגמינן ולא תיכול קורצין, ואומר אני שכן היתה דת של הולכי רכיל לאכול לגימא במקום שמלשינין שם והוא סימן קיום דברים שמאותה שעה יש עליהם לברר דבריהם ולאמת לשון הרע שאמרו ואותה סעודה נקראת אכילת קורצין לשון קורץ בעיניו (משלי ו׳:י״ג) שהוא לסימן לשון הרע:
rashi.eng: *some Chaldean men approached and denounced.* Aram. וַאֲכַלוּ קַרְצֵיהוֹן informed about them. (Lev. 19:16) “Do not go as a talebearer among your people,” is translated by Targum as קוּרצִין לָא תֵיכוּ I say that it was the custom of talebearers to eat a meal in the place where they informed, and that was a sign of the verification of their words; for at that time it was incumbent upon them to clarify their words and to verify the slander that they spoke, and that meal was called eating קוּרצִין, an expression of (Prov. 6:13) “he winks (קוֹרֵץ) with his eyes,” which is a sign of slander.

notes.153: (tn): Aram “answered and said,” a common Aramaic idiom that occurs repeatedly in this chapter.
notes.154: (sn): O king, live forever! is a comment of typical court courtesy that is not necessarily indicative of the real sentiments of the speaker. Ancient oriental court protocol could sometimes require a certain amount of hypocrisy.

rashi.heb:
*ענו ואמרין.* 
צוחו כל עניה שבמקרא לשון קול רם הוא:
rashi.eng: *They spoke up and said.* Aram. עֲנוֹ, they shouted. Every [expression of] עֲנִיָה in Scriptures is an expression of raising the voice.

rashi.heb:
*שמת טעם.* 
גזרת דבר:
rashi.eng: *gave an order.* issued a decree.

notes.155: (sn): Daniel’s absence from this scene has sparked the imagination of commentators, some of whom have suggested that perhaps he was unable to attend the dedication due to sickness or due to being away on business. Hippolytus supposed that Daniel may have been watching from a distance.

rashi.heb:
*איתי.* 
יש:
rashi.eng: *There are.* Aram. אִיתַי

rashi.heb:
*יהודאין.* 
משבט יהודה:
rashi.eng: *Judahite men.* of the tribe of Judah.

rashi.heb:
*אלך.* 
אלה: לא שמו:
rashi.eng: *these.* Aram. אִלֵּךְ

rashi.heb:
*עלך מלכא טעם.* 
לא חשו לתת עצה לעצמן לחוש על גזרותיך:
rashi.eng: *did not take counsel to follow your decree.* Aram. עֲלָיִךְ מַלְכָּא טְעֵם לָא שָּׂמוּ. They did not care to give themselves counsel to care for your decrees.

notes.156: (tn): Aram “in anger and wrath”; NASB “in rage and anger.” The expression is a hendiadys.
notes.158: (tn): Aram “these men.” The pronoun is used in the translation to avoid undue repetition.

rashi.heb:
*אמר להיתיה.* 
צוה להביא:
rashi.eng: *ordered to bring.* [as translated,] ordered to bring.

rashi.heb:
*היתיו.* 
הובאו:
rashi.eng: *were brought.* [as translated,] were brought.

rashi.heb:
*הצדא.* 
שמא גזרותי צדו ושממה ודבר רק היא בעיניכם אתם שדרך מישך ועבד נגו אשר לאלוהי אינכם עובדים, ה"א של הצדא משמשת בלשון תמיהה:
rashi.eng: *Is it meaningless.* Aram. הַצְדָא. Are my decrees void and desolate and an empty thing in your eyes, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you do not worship my god? The “hey” of הַצְדָא is used as an interrogative expression.

rashi.heb:
*די הקמת.* 
שהקמותי:
rashi.eng: *that I have set up.* [as translated,] that I have set up.

rashi.heb:
*כען הן איתיכון עתידין.* 
עתה הנכם עתידים על כרחכם לקבל זו עליכם:
rashi.eng: *Now, behold you are destined.* Now, behold you are destined against your will to accept this upon yourselves.

rashi.heb:
*והן לא תסגדון.* 
ואם לא תשתחוו תהיו מושלכים:
rashi.eng: *and if you do not prostrate yourselves.* and if you do not prostrate yourselves, you shall be cast.

rashi.heb:
*לגו.* 
לתוך:
rashi.eng: *into.* into the midst of.

rashi.heb:
*ומן הוא אלה.* 
ומי הוא שום אלוה שיציל אתכם מידי:
rashi.eng: *and who is a god.* and who is a god who will save you from my hands?

notes.160: (tc): In the MT this word is understood to begin the following address (“answered and said to the king, ‘O Nebuchadnezzar’”). However, it seems unlikely that Nebuchadnezzar’s subordinates would address the king in such a familiar way, particularly in light of the danger that they now found themselves in. The present translation implies moving the atnach from “king” to “Nebuchadnezzar.”
notes.161: (tn): Aram “to return a word to you.”

rashi.heb:
*למלכא נבוכדנצר.* 
למה הוזכר שמו אלא כך אמרו לו אם לקבל עלינו גזירתך לתת מסין וארנוניות וגולגליות אתה מלך עלינו אם לכפור בהקב"ה נבוכדנצר שפל אנשים בעינינו ובזוי עם אתה:
rashi.eng: *to the king, ‘Nebuchadnezzar.* Why is his name mentioned? But this is what they said to him: “If [it concerns] taking upon ourselves to pay taxes, either the tax from the crops or the head taxes, you are king over us, [but] if [it concerns] denying the Holy One, blessed be He, [you are merely] Nebuchadnezzar. In our eyes, you are a lowly person and the most despised of the people. You and a dog are equal.”

rashi.heb:
*לא חשחין אנחנא.* 
לא חוששין אנו על זאת ליטול עצה מה להשיבך כי המענה מוכן ושגור בפינו:
rashi.eng: *we do not care.* We do not care to take counsel on what to answer you, for the answer is ready and fluent in our mouths.

notes.162: (tc): The ancient versions typically avoid the conditional element of v. 17.
notes.163: (tn): The Aramaic expression used here is very difficult to interpret. The question concerns the meaning and syntax of אִיתַי (’itay, “is” or “exist”). There are several possibilities. (1) Some interpreters take this word closely with the participle later in the verse יָכִל (yakhil, “able”), understanding the two words to form a periphrastic construction (“if our God is…able”; cf. H. Bauer and P. Leander, Grammatik des Biblisch-Aram�ischen, 365, �111b). But the separation of the two elements from one another is not an argument in favor of this understanding. (2) Other interpreters take the first part of v. 17 to mean “If it is so, then our God will deliver us” (cf. KJV, ASV, RSV, NASB). However, the normal sense of ’itay is existence; on this point see F. Rosenthal, Grammar, 45, �95. The present translation maintains the sense of existence for the verb (“If our God…exists”), even though the statement is admittedly difficult to understand in this light. The statement may be an implicit reference back to Nebuchadnezzar’s comment in v. 15, which denies the existence of a god capable of delivering from the king’s power.

rashi.heb:
*יכיל לשזבותנא.* 
יכול להצילנו מכל צרה:
rashi.eng: *He can save us.* He can save us from all our troubles.

rashi.heb:
*מן אתון נורא.* 
ומן ידך מלכא ישזיב מן הכבשן ומן ידך יציל:
rashi.eng: *From the burning fiery furnace and from your hands, O king, He will save us.* from the furnace and from your hands He will save.

rashi.heb:
*והן לא.* 
ואם לא יחפוץ להציל גופינו ידיע להוי לך:
rashi.eng: *And if not.* And if He will not wish to save our bodies, let it be known to you, etc.

notes.164: (tn): Aram “the appearance of his face was altered”; cf. NLT “his face became distorted with rage”; NAB “[his] face became livid with utter rage.”

rashi.heb:
*התמלי חמא.* 
נתמלא חמה:
rashi.eng: *was filled with wrath.* [as translated,] was filled with wrath.

rashi.heb:
*וצלם אנפוהי אשתני.* 
ופרצוף פניו נשתנו:
rashi.eng: *and the features of his face changed.* [as translated,] and the features of his face changed.

rashi.heb:
*למזא לאתונא.* 
להצית לכבשן האש ולחממו:
rashi.eng: *to heat the furnace.* to light the fiery furnace and to heat it.

rashi.heb:
*חד שבעה על די חזה למזיה.* 
על אחת שבע פעמים ששיערוהו עד כדי הסיקו וכאילו יבעירוהו ז' שיעורין כמוהו:
rashi.eng: *seven times as much as it should be heated.* instead of once, seven times as much as they calculated to heat it up; and it was as though they would kindle it seven times as much as it required.

rashi.heb:
*למזיה.* 
להסיקו:
rashi.eng: *to be heated.* lit. to heat it.

notes.166: (tn): This is sometimes taken as a comparative: “[some of the] strongest.”

rashi.heb:
*ולגבורין גברי חיל די בחיליה.* 
ולאנשים גבורי כח אשר בחילו:
rashi.eng: *certain mighty men in his army.* [as translated,] certain mighty men in his army.

rashi.heb:
*אמר לכפתה.* 
צוה לאסור אותם שראה מתחזקים לענותו קשות ואמר גבורים הם אלו וצוה לגבורים אשר בחילו לאסור אותם:
rashi.eng: *And he commanded… to bind.* He commanded to bind them because he saw that they were strengthening themselves to answer him harshly, and he said, “These are mighty”; so he commanded the mighty men in his army to bind them.

notes.167: (sn): There is a great deal of uncertainty with regard to the specific nature of these items of clothing.
notes.168: (tn): Aram “into the midst of the furnace.” For stylistic reasons the words “the midst of” have been left untranslated.

rashi.heb:
*גובריא אלך.* 
אנשים אלו:
rashi.eng: *these men.* [as translated,] these men.

rashi.heb:
*כפיתו בסרבליהון.* 
נתקשרו בבגדי מעטפותן:
rashi.eng: *were bound in their cloaks.* They were bound in the garments in which they enwrapped themselves.

rashi.heb:
*פטשיהון וכרבלתהון.* 
מיני מלבוש מלכות שהיה להם ואע"פ שהיו יוצאין לידון לפני נ"נ דיני מיתה לא שנו בגדיהם להשפיל את גדולתם מכאן למדו חכמים שאפי' בשעת הסכנה לא ישנה אדם מן השררה שהוחזק בה:
rashi.eng: *their trousers, their robes.* types of royal raiment that they had; and although they were going forth to be judged before Nebuchadnezzar regarding their death sentence, they did not change their clothes to humble their greatness. From here the Sages learned that even in times of danger, a person should not change from the ruling position to which he has become accustomed.

rashi.heb:
*וכרבלתהון.* 
יש לו דוגמא (בד"ה א' טו) ודוד מכורבל:
rashi.eng: *their robes.* Aram. וְכַרְבְּלָתְהוֹן. There is a word similar to this (in I Chron. 15:27): "And David was clothed (מְכֻרְבָּל).

rashi.heb:
*ורמיו לגוא אתון נורא.* 
והושלכו לתוך כבשן בוערה:
rashi.eng: *and they were cast into the burning, fiery furnce.* [as translated,] and they were cast into the burning, fiery furnace.

notes.171: (tn): Aram “the flame of the fire” (so KJV, ASV, NASB); NRSV “the raging flames.”

rashi.heb:
*כל קבל דנה.* 
כל עומת זאת אשר מצות המלך היתה עזה:
rashi.eng: *In view of this.* in view of this, that the king’s command was strong.

rashi.heb:
*ואתונא אזה יתירא.* 
והכבשן הוסק מאד:
rashi.eng: *and the furnace was heated excessively.* and the furnace was heated to a great degree.

rashi.heb:
*גובריא אלך.* 
אלו האנשים הגבורים אשר קשרו את חנניה מישאל ועזריה והשליכום לכבשן:
rashi.eng: *these men.* these mighty men who had bound Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah and had cast them into the furnace.

rashi.heb:
*קטיל המון שביבא די נורא.* 
שרף אותם כח שביב האש:
rashi.eng: *were killed by a spark of fire.* The power of a spark of fire burned them.

notes.172: (tn): Aram “into the midst of the furnace.” For stylistic reasons the words “the midst of” have been left untranslated.
notes.173: (sn): The deuterocanonical writings known as The Prayer of Azariah and The Song of the Three present at this point a confession and petition for God’s forgiveness and a celebration of God’s grace for the three Jewish youths in the fiery furnace. Though not found in the Hebrew/Aramaic text of Daniel, these compositions do appear in the ancient Greek versions.

rashi.heb:
*מכפתין.* 
קשורין:
rashi.eng: *bound.* [as translated,] bound.

rashi.heb:
*תוה.* 
תמה:
rashi.eng: *was bewildered.* Aram. תְּוַהּ, wondered.

rashi.heb:
*וקם בהתבהלה.* 
ועמד בבהלה:
rashi.eng: *and stood up in haste.* Aram. וְקָם בְּהִתְבְּהָלָה.

rashi.heb:
*ענין ואמרין.* 
עונין ואומרי' למלך:
rashi.eng: *answered and said.* Aram. עָנַיִן וְאָמְרִין They answered and said to the king.

rashi.heb:
*יציבא מלכא.* 
אמת דבר המלך:
rashi.eng: *The king is true.* Aram. יַצִיבָא מַלְכָּא The king has spoken the truth.

notes.176: (sn): The phrase like that of a god is in Aramaic “like that of a son of the gods.” Many patristic writers understood this phrase in a christological sense (i.e., “the Son of God”). But it should be remembered that these are words spoken by a pagan who is seeking to explain things from his own polytheistic frame of reference; for him the phrase “like a son of the gods” is equivalent to “like a divine being.”

rashi.heb:
*שרין מהלכין בגוא נורא.* 
מותרין מאסוריהן והולכים בתוך האש:
rashi.eng: *free men walking in the midst of the fire.* freed from their bonds and walking in the midst of the fire.

rashi.heb:
*וחבל לא איתי בהון.* 
וחבלה לא יש בהם:
rashi.eng: *and there is no wound upon them.* [as translated,] and there is no wound upon them.

rashi.heb:
*ורוה די.* 
רביעאה ותוארו של רביעי:
rashi.eng: *and the form of the fourth.* [as translated,] and the form of the fourth.

rashi.heb:
*דמה לבר אלהין.* 
דומה למלאך שראיתי בהיותי עם סנחרב כשנשרפו אוכלוסיו שנאמר (ישעיהו ל״ז:ל״ו) ויך במחנה אשור ונבוכדנצר היה שם ונמלט בתוך עשרה שנמלטו מהם:
rashi.eng: *is like [that of] an angel.* It is like the angel I saw when I was with Sannecherib, when his armies were burned, as it is said (II Kings 19:35): “[And an angel of the Lord went forth] and slew… of the camp of Assyria.” And Nebuchadnezzar was there and fled among the ten who fled from them.

notes.178: (tn): Aram “from the midst of the fire.” For stylistic reasons the words “the midst of” have been left untranslated.

rashi.heb:
*קרב.* 
לתרע אתון נורא נגש לשער החצר שהכבשן בתוכה לדבר עמהם ומתחלה היה רואה אותם מרחוק:
rashi.eng: *approached the gate of the… fiery furnace.* He approached the gate of the court, in which the furnace was situated, to speak with them, and at first, he saw them from afar.

rashi.heb:
*פוקו ואתו.* 
צאו ובאו ולא אמר להם עלו ובואו מכאן למדנו שצף קרקעית הכבשן והשוה לארץ שלא יטרחו לעלות:
rashi.eng: *Step out and come.* “step out and come,” but he did not say to them, “step out and ascend.” From here we learn that the floor of the furnace floated up and became even with the ground, so that they should not be troubled to go up.

rashi.heb:
*באדין נפקון.* 
אע"פ שבטוחין בנס העשוי להם לא מלאה לבם לזלזל במלכות לצאת שלא ברשות:
rashi.eng: *Then… came out.* Although they were confident of the miracle that had been performed for them, they did not dare to treat the king lightly, to go out without permission.

notes.180: (tn): Aram “the fire did not have power.”

rashi.heb:
*ומתכנשין אחשדרפניא.* 
ד' אומות נמנו למעלה באסיפה הראשונה שלא נמנו כאן אדרגזריא דתבריא גדבריא תפתיא הם גבורי החיל אשר הרגם שביב האש בהשליכם את חנניה וחבריו לאור:
rashi.eng: *And the satraps… gathered.* Four nations were counted above in the first gathering who were not counted here: Adargazeria, Dethaveria, Gedaveria, Tiftaei. They are the mighty men whom the spark of fire had killed when they cast Hananiah and his colleagues into the fire.

rashi.heb:
*חזין לגובריא אלך.* 
רואין את האנשים האלה חנניה וחבריו:
rashi.eng: *saw these men.* saw these men: Hananiah and his colleagues.

rashi.heb:
*די לא שלט נורא בגשמהון.* 
אשר לא שלטה האש בגופם:
rashi.eng: *that the fire had taken no effect on their bodies.* [as translated,] that the fire had taken no effect on their bodies.

rashi.heb:
*גשמהון.* 
גופן בל' ארמי ויש רבים בזה הספר:
rashi.eng: *on their bodies.* בְּגֶשְּׁמְהוֹן, their bodies, in Aramaic, and there are many [instances of it] in this Book.

rashi.heb:
*ושער ראשיהון לא התחרך.* 
שער ראשיהון לא נחרך:
rashi.eng: *the hair of their heads was not singed.* [as translated,] the hair of their heads was not singed.

rashi.heb:
*לא שנו.* 
לא נשתנו ממראיתן:
rashi.eng: *their robes were not changed.* They did not change from their appearance.

rashi.heb:
*לא עדת בהון.* 
לא סרה לתוכם:
rashi.eng: *and the smell of fire had not been absorbed by them.* Aram. לָא עֲדַת בְּהוֹן, did not pass into their midst.

notes.182: (sn): The king identifies the “son of the gods” (v. 25) as an angel. Comparable Hebrew expressions are used elsewhere in the Hebrew Bible for the members of God’s angelic assembly (see Gen 6:2, 4; Job 1:6; 2:1; 38:7; Pss 29:1; 89:6). An angel later comes to rescue Daniel from the lions (Dan 6:22).

rashi.heb:
*ענה נבוכדנצר.* 
צוח נבוכדנצר:
rashi.eng: *Nebuchadnezzar cried out.* [as translated,] Nebuchadnezzar cried out.

rashi.heb:
*די התרחיצו עלוהי.* 
אשר בטחו עליו:
rashi.eng: *who trusted him.* [as translated,] who trusted him.

rashi.heb:
*ומלת מלכא שניו.* 
ומלת המלך שנו שלא לקיימו:
rashi.eng: *deviated from the command of the king.* They deviated from the king’s command by not fulfilling it.

rashi.heb:
*ויהבו גשמהון.* 
ומסרו גופם:
rashi.eng: *and risked their lives.* lit. delivered their bodies.

rashi.heb:
*לאלההון.* 
זולתי לאלהיהם:
rashi.eng: *except to their God.* [as translated,] except to their God.

notes.185: (tn): Aram “from me is placed an edict.”

rashi.heb:
*שים טעם.* 
כלומר יושם חק:
rashi.eng: *Now an order is issued by me.* [as translated,] Now an order is issued by me.

rashi.heb:
*די יאמר.* 
שלו אשר יאמר משגה כלומר שום דבר של גנאי:
rashi.eng: *that will speak amiss.* that will speak in error, i.e., any disrespectful word.

rashi.heb:
*הדמין.* 
אברים כלומר ינתחוהו לאברים:
rashi.eng: *limb from limb.* Aram הַּדָּמִין limbs; i.e., they will cut him into limbs.

rashi.heb:
*נולי ישתוה.* 
אשפה יושם:
rashi.eng: *shall be made a dungheap.* [as translated,] shall be made a dungheap.

rashi.heb:
*די יכול להצלה כדנה.* 
אשר יכול להציל כזאת:
rashi.eng: *that can save in this manner.* [as translated,] that can save in this manner.

notes.187: (tn): Aram “and the king.” The proper name has been supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*הצלח.* 
הצליח והגדיל אותם:
rashi.eng: *made… prosper.* made them prosper and aggrandized them.

rashi.heb:
*נבוכדנצר מלכא לכל עממיא.* 
זה טופס כתב האגרת נבוכדנצר המלך שואל לשלום לכל העמים:
rashi.eng: *King Nebuchadnezzar [says] to all peoples.* This is the text of the missive: King Nebuchadnezzar greets all peoples.

rashi.heb:
*שפר קדמי להחויה.* 
טוב לי להגיד:
rashi.eng: *it behooves me to recite.* It is good for me to tell.

notes.188: (sn): Beginning with , the verse numbers through in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Aramaic text (BHS), with ET = AT, ET = AT, ET = AT, ET = AT, etc., through ET = AT. Thus Dan 3:31-33 of the Aramaic text appears as Dan 4:1-3 in the English Bible, and the corresponding verses of ch. 4 differ accordingly. In spite of the division of the Aramaic text, a good case can be made that 3:31-33 AT (= 4:1-3 ET) is actually the introduction to ch. 4.

rashi.heb:
*שלה הוית בביתי.* 
שליו הייתי:
rashi.eng: *was tranquil in my house.* [as translated,] was tranquil in my house.

rashi.heb:
*וידחלנני.* 
ואיים עלי והפחדני:
rashi.eng: *and it frightened me.* It brought upon me fear and fright.

notes.190: (tn): Aram “his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom.”

notes.191: (sn): This verse marks the beginning of chap. 4 in the Aramaic text of Daniel (see the note on ). The Greek OT (LXX) has the following addition: “In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign he said.” This date would suggest a link to the destruction of Jerusalem in 586 B.C. In general, the LXX of chapters 4-6 is very different from the MT, so much so that the following notes will call attention only to selected readings. In Daniel 4 the LXX lacks sizable portions of material in the MT (e.g., vv. 3-6, 31-32), includes sizable portions of material not in the MT (e.g., v. 14a, parts of vv. 16, 28), has a different order of some material (e.g., v. 8 after v. 9), and in some instances is vastly different from the MT (e.g., vv. 30, 34). Whether these differences are due to an excessively paraphrastic translation technique adopted for these chapters in the LXX, or are due to differences in the underlying Vorlage of the LXX, is a disputed matter. The latter seems more likely. There is a growing trend in modern scholarship to take the LXX of chapters 4-6 much more seriously than was the case in most earlier text-critical studies that considered this issue.

rashi.heb:
*ועד אחרן.* 
ועד אשר באחרונה הובא לפני דניאל:
rashi.eng: *Until, at last,.* until, at last, Daniel was brought in before me.

rashi.heb:
*כשום אלהי.* 
עכו"ם של בבל בל שמה טשצר שם לשון חכמה הוא באומות:
rashi.eng: *like the name of my god.* The deity of Babylon was named Bel. Teshazzar is the name of an expression of wisdom in Aramaic.

notes.195: (tn): Aram “from me there was placed a decree.”
notes.196: (tn): The Aramaic infinitive here is active.

rashi.heb:
*וכל רז לא אנס לך.* 
וכל סתום לא נאנס ולא נכחד ממך:
rashi.eng: *and no secret is hidden from you.* No mystery is robbed [from you] or denied you.

notes.197: (sn): This explanation of the meaning of the name Belteshazzar may be more of a paronomasia than a strict etymology.

rashi.heb:
*רבה אילנא ותקיף.* 
גדל האילן והוחזק ועצם:
rashi.eng: *The tree grew and became strong.* The tree grew and became stronger and stronger.

rashi.heb:
*ימטא לשמיא.* 
הגיע השמים:
rashi.eng: *reached the sky.* [as translated,] reached the sky.

notes.198: (tc): The present translation assumes the reading חֲזִי (khazi, “consider”) rather than the MT חֶזְוֵי (khezvey, “visions”). The MT implies that the king required Daniel to disclose both the dream and its interpretation, as in chapter 2. But in the following verses Nebuchadnezzar recounts his dream, while Daniel presents only its interpretation.

rashi.heb:
*עפיה שפיר.* 
ענפו נאה:
rashi.eng: *its branches were beautiful.* [as translated,] its branches were beautiful.

rashi.heb:
*ואנבה שגיא.* 
פריו רב:
rashi.eng: *and its fruit was plentiful.* [as translated,] and its fruit was plentiful.

rashi.heb:
*מזון לכולא ביה.* 
וכדי מזון לכל בריה היה בו:
rashi.eng: *and on it was sustenance for all.* On it was enough sustenance for all

rashi.heb:
*תטלל.* 
לשון צל:
rashi.eng: *took shade.* Aram. תַּטְלֵל, an expression of shade.

rashi.heb:
*ידורון.* 
ל' מדור ולינה:
rashi.eng: *dwelt.* Aram. יְדֻרָן, an expression of dwelling and lodging.

rashi.heb:
*יתזון.* 
ל' מזון:
rashi.eng: *was nourished.* Aram. יִתְּזִין, an expression of food.

notes.199: (tc): The LXX lacks the first two words (Aram “the visions of my head”) of the Aramaic text.
notes.200: (tn): Instead of “in the middle of the land,” some English versions render this phrase “a tree at the center of the earth” (NRSV); NAB, CEV “of the world”; NLT “in the middle of the earth.” The Hebrew phrase can have either meaning.

rashi.heb:
*חזה הוית.* 
רואה הייתי:
rashi.eng: *I saw.* lit. I was seeing.

rashi.heb:
*ואלו עיר וקדיש.* 
והנה מלאך שהוא ער לעולם וקדוש:
rashi.eng: *and behold a wakeful holy one.* i.e., an angel who is forever awake and holy.

notes.203: (tn): Or “to the end of all the earth” (so KJV, ASV); NCV, CEV “from anywhere on earth.”

rashi.heb:
*קרא בחיל.* 
צועק בכח:
rashi.eng: *Crying out loudly.* crying with might.

rashi.heb:
*גודו אילנא.* 
קוצו האילן:
rashi.eng: *Cut down the tree… shake off its branches.* shake off and cause its branches to fall.

rashi.heb:
*אתרו עפייה.* 
השירו והפילו ענפיו:
rashi.eng: *shake off its branches.* shake off and cause its branches to fall.

rashi.heb:
*ובדרו אנבה.* 
הפיצו פריו:
rashi.eng: *and scatter its fruit.* [as translated,] and scatter its fruit.

rashi.heb:
*תנוד חיותא מן תחתוהי.* 
ינודו החיות מתחתיו:
rashi.eng: *the beasts shall wander away from beneath it.* [as translated,] the beasts shall wander away from beneath it.

rashi.heb:
*ברם עיקר שרשוהי בארעא שבוקו.* 
אך עיקר שרשיו הניחו:
rashi.eng: *But leave its main roots in the ground.* but its main roots leave over.

rashi.heb:
*ובאסור די פרזל ונחש.* 
כלו' תנו רגליו בכבלי ברזל כשם שעושין לסוס שמניחין אותו באפר כך כבלוהי בכבלי':
rashi.eng: *and in fetters of iron and copper.* i.e., place his feet in iron fetters as is done to a horse that is left in the meadow; so shall you chain him with fetters.

rashi.heb:
*בדתאא.* 
בעשב השדה כלומר באחו שלא יזוז משם:
rashi.eng: *in the grass.* Aram. בְדִתְאָא in the grass of the field, i.e., in the meadow, so that he should not move from there.

rashi.heb:
*יצטבע.* 
יהא שרוי תמיד לשון טבילה:
rashi.eng: *it shall be drenched.* Aram.

rashi.heb:
*חלקה.* 
חלקו:
rashi.eng: *its lot.* [as translated,] its lot. יִצְטַבַּע, it shall always be drenched, an expression of immersion.

notes.207: (tn): Aram “a watcher and a holy one.” The expression is a hendiadys; so also in v. 23. This “watcher” is apparently an angel. The Greek OT (LXX) in fact has ἄγγελος (angelo", “angel”) here. Theodotion simply transliterates the Aramaic word (’ir). The term is sometimes rendered “sentinel” (NAB) or “messenger” (NIV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*ושבעה עדנין.* 
שבע שנים:
rashi.eng: *and seven periods.* seven years.

rashi.heb:
*יחלפון עלוהי.* 
יעברו עליו בגזרה זו:
rashi.eng: *will pass over him.* will pass over him with this decree.

rashi.heb:
*שאלתא.* 
גזרה וע"י שנמלכין בהקב"ה קודם שיגזרו הגזרה קורא אותה שאלתא:
rashi.eng: *the edict.* a decree, but since they take counsel from the Holy One, blessed be He, before they issue the decree, he calls it a question.

rashi.heb:
*עד דברת.* 
כמו למען:
rashi.eng: *in order that.* Aram. עַד דִּבְרַת, like לְמַעַן.

rashi.heb:
*די ינדעון חייא.* 
שידעו כל החיים:
rashi.eng: *that the living should know.* in order that all the living should know.

rashi.heb:
*ולמן די יצבא.* 
למי שירצה:
rashi.eng: *and to whom He wishes.* [as translated,] and to whom He wishes.

notes.210: (tn): Aram “the stock of its root.” So also v. 23. The implication here is that although the tree is chopped down, it is not killed. Its life-giving root is spared. The application to Nebuchadnezzar is obvious.
notes.211: (sn): The function of the band of iron and bronze is not entirely clear, but it may have had to do with preventing the splitting or further deterioration of the portion of the tree that was left after being chopped down. By application it would then refer to the preservation of Nebuchadnezzar’s life during the time of his insanity.

rashi.heb:
*פשרא.* 
פתרונו:
rashi.eng: *its interpretation.* [as translated,] its interpretation.

rashi.heb:
*ואנת כהל.* 
ואתה יכול:
rashi.eng: *but you can.* [as translated,] but you can.

notes.213: (tn): Aram “its heart.” The metaphor of the tree begins to fade here and the reality behind the symbol (the king) begins to emerge.
notes.214: (sn): The seven periods of time probably refer to seven years.

rashi.heb:
*אדין דניאל.* 
אשתומם שתק:
rashi.eng: *Then Daniel, whose name is Belteshazzar, was bewildered.* He was silent.

rashi.heb:
*ורעינוהי.* 
ומחשבותיו:
rashi.eng: *and his thoughts.* [as translated,] and his thoughts.

rashi.heb:
*יבהלוניה.* 
שהיה ירא לפתור לו חלום:
rashi.eng: *alarmed him.* for he was afraid to interpret the dream for him.

rashi.heb:
*מרי.* 
אדוני, אמרו רבותינו מארי חלמא לשנאך קדש הוא תלה עיניו להקב"ה ואמר חלום זה יתקיים על שנאך זה וא"ת לנבוכדנצר אמר והלא ישראל שונאו אפשר שיקללם:
rashi.eng: *My lord.* Aram. מָרִאי. Our Rabbis said (Shevu. 35b): “My Lord, may the dream be for Your enemies,” refers to God.
