He raised his eyes to the Holy One, blessed be He, and said, “May this dream be fulfilled upon this enemy of Yours.” But if you say that he said it to Nebuchadnezzar, was not Israel his enemy? Is it possible that he would curse them?

rashi.heb:
*לערך.* 
לשונאך כמו ויהי ערך (שמואל א כה):
rashi.eng: *for your foes.* Aram. לְעָרָךְ, like (Sam. 28:16): “and has become [the supporter of] your foes (עָרֶךָ).”

notes.216: (tc): The present translation follows an underlying reading of עַל־דִּבְרַת (’al-divrat, “so that”) rather than MT עַד־דִּבְרַת (’ad-divrat, “until”).
notes.217: (tn): Aram “the kingdom of man”; NASB “the realm of mankind”; NCV “every kingdom on earth.”

notes.218: (tc): The present translation reads פִּשְׁרֵהּ (pishreh, “its interpretation”) with the Qere and many medieval Hebrew MSS; the Kethib is פִּשְׁרָא (pishra’, “the interpretation”); so also v. 16.

notes.220: (tn): Aram “about one hour.” The expression refers idiomatically to a brief period of time of undetermined length.

notes.223: (tn): Aram “the beasts of the field” (also in vv. 23, 25, 32).

rashi.heb:
*די מטת על: מרי מלכא.* 
אשר הגיע על אדוני המלך:
rashi.eng: *which befalls my lord, the king.* [as translated,] which befalls my lord, the king.

notes.224: (sn): Much of modern scholarship views this chapter as a distortion of traditions that were originally associated with Nabonidus rather than with Nebuchadnezzar. A Qumran text, the Prayer of Nabonidus, is often cited for parallels to these events.

rashi.heb:
*ולך טרדין מן אנשא.* 
ואותך יטרדו מבני אדם:
rashi.eng: *And they will banish you from mankind.* [as translated,] and they will banish you from mankind.

rashi.heb:
*לך מצבעין.* 
אותך יטבלו:
rashi.eng: *and with the dew of the heavens you shall be drenched.* They will immerse you.

rashi.heb:
*ושבעה עדנין יחלפון עלך.* 
יש לומר גמול בה"מ שהחריב שנבנתה בשבע שנים:
rashi.eng: *and seven periods shall pass over you.* We may say that this is the recompense for the Temple, which he destroyed, which was built in seven years.

rashi.heb:
*ודי אמרו וגו'.* 
אשר אמרו להניח שרשוהי של אילן והוא הפתרון מלכותא לך קיימת. המלכות עומדת לך סופך שתשוב לך מלכותך:
rashi.eng: *And what they said, etc..* What they said-to leave the roots of the tree-this is the interpretation: מַלְכוּתָךְ, your kingdom-will remain yours. Your kingdom will ultimately be restored to you.

rashi.heb:
*מן די תנדע די שליטין שמיא.* 
מאחר שתדע שהעליונים מושלים בעולם:
rashi.eng: *as soon as you know that Heaven rules.* as soon as you know that the heavenly beings rule over the world.

rashi.heb:
*להן מלכא.* 
באמת אתה מלך שמע לעצתי:
rashi.eng: *Indeed, O king.* Indeed, O king, hearken to my counsel.

rashi.heb:
*מלכי.* 
עצתי כמו איעצך אמלכינך:
rashi.eng: *my counsel.* Aram. מִלְכִּי, my counsel, like (Num. 24:14): “I shall advise you (אִיעָצְךְ),” which is translated: אֲמַלְּכִינָךְ.

rashi.heb:
*ישפר עלך.* 
עצתי תיטב בעיניך לשמוע מילי:
rashi.eng: *please you.* May my counsel please you that you hearken to my words.

rashi.heb:
*וחטאך בצדקה פרוק.* 
וחטאתך בצדקה פרוק מעל צוארך:
rashi.eng: *and with charity you will remove your sin.* With charity, break your sin off your neck.

rashi.heb:
*ועויתך במחן ענין.* 
ועונותיך פרוק בחנינת עניים:
rashi.eng: *and your iniquity by showing mercy to poor.* and remove your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor.

rashi.heb:
*הן תהוה ארכא לשלותך.* 
אולי תהא שהות לשלומך שלא תמהר הרעה לבא ומה ראה דניאל להשיא עצה טובה לנבוכדנצר ראה ישראל עניים שפלי גולה מחזירין על הפתחים והשיאו עצה לחננם אמר לו עניים אלו שהגליתם רעבים הם פרנסם וכן עשה פתח אוצרותיו והיה מפרנסם כל י"ב חדש:
rashi.eng: *perhaps your tranquility will last.* Perhaps there will be time for your tranquility, that the evil should not come swiftly. Now what did Daniel see to give Nebuchadnezzar good advice? He saw the Jews poor and humbled by the exile, going from door to door begging for alms, and he gave him advice to deal mercifully with them. He said to him, “These poor people whom you exiled are hungry; nourish them.” And so he did. He opened his storehouses and fed them for a full twelve months.

notes.225: (tn): The Aramaic indefinite active plural is used here like the English passive. So also in v. 28, 29,32.
notes.226: (tn): Aram “from mankind.” So also in v. 32.
notes.227: (tn): Aram “your dwelling will be.” So also in v. 32.
notes.229: (sn): Nebuchadnezzar’s insanity has features that are associated with the mental disorder known as boanthropy, in which the person so afflicted imagines himself to be an ox or a similar animal and behaves accordingly.

rashi.heb:
*כלא מטא.* 
כל הפתרון הגיע על נבוכדנצר:
rashi.eng: *All this befell.* The entire interpretation befell Nebuchadnezzar.

notes.231: (sn): The reference to heaven here is a circumlocution for God. There was a tendency in Jewish contexts to avoid direct reference to God. Cf. the expression “kingdom of heaven” in the NT and such statements as “I have sinned against heaven and in your sight” (Luke 15:21).

rashi.heb:
*מהלך הוה.* 
הולך היה:
rashi.eng: *he was walking.* [as translated,] he was walking.

notes.232: (tn): Aram “if there may be a lengthening to your prosperity.”

rashi.heb:
*הלא דא היא.* 
שמע עניים באים על הפתח וצועקים אמר מה קול ההמון הזה באזני אמרו לו עבדיו אלו העניים שקבעת להם עת פרנסתם אמר הלא דא היא בבל רבתא וגומר ואלמלא ביזבזתי אוצרותי לפרנסת עניים מהיכן הייתי בונה כל הפלטרין הללו מעתה איני מפרנסם כך דרש רבי תנחומא:
rashi.eng: *Is this not.* He heard poor people coming to the door and crying out. He said, “What is the sound of this multitude in my ears?” His servants said to him, “These are the poor for whom you arranged a time to feed.” He said, “Is this not the great Babylon, etc. If I had squandered my storehouses, from where would I have built all these palaces? From now on, I shall not feed them.” Rabbi Tanhuma (Mishpatim 4) explained it in this manner.

rashi.heb:
*וליקר הדרי.* 
ולכבוד תפארתי:
rashi.eng: *and for the honor of my glory.* [as translated,] and for the honor of my glory.

rashi.heb:
*עוד מלתא בפום מלכא,: עדת מנך.* 
סרה מנך:
rashi.eng: *has turned away from you.* [as translated,] has turned away from you.

notes.234: (tn): The word “battlements” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied from context. Many English versions supply “roof” here (e.g., NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV); cf. NLT “on the flat roof.”

rashi.heb:
*טרדין.* 
לשון גירושין:
rashi.eng: *they will banish.* Aram. טָרְדִין. an expression of driving away.

notes.236: (tn): Aram “by the might of my strength.”

rashi.heb:
*ספת.* 
הגזירה כלתה עליו:
rashi.eng: *was fulfilled.* The decree was executed upon him.

rashi.heb:
*גשמה.* 
גופיה:

*שערה כנשרין רבה.* 
שערותיו ככנפי נשרים גדלו על כל גופו:
rashi.eng: *his hair grew like [the feathers of] eagles.* His hair grew over his entire body like eagles’ feathers.

rashi.heb:
*וטפרוהי כצפרין.* 
וצפרניו כצפור:
rashi.eng: *and his nails like birds.* and his nails were like a bird’s [talons].

notes.237: (tn): Aram “in the mouth of the king.”

rashi.heb:
*ולקצת יומיא.* 
לקץ הימים שקבעו לו לסוף ז' השנים:
rashi.eng: *And at the end of the days.* at the end of the days that were set for him; at the end of the seven years.

rashi.heb:
*נטלת.* 
נשאתי:
rashi.eng: *raised.* [as translated,] raised.

rashi.heb:
*ומנדעי עלי יתיב.* 
ודעתי עלי חזרה:
rashi.eng: *and my understanding was restored to me.* [as translated,] and my understanding was restored to me.

rashi.heb:
*ולעלאה ברכת.* 
ואת העליון ברכתי:
rashi.eng: *and I blessed the Most High.* [as translated,] and I blessed the Most High.

rashi.heb:
*כלה חשיבין.* 
רבותינו אמרו האי חירגא דיומא לא שמיה אבק הנראה בשמש:
rashi.eng: *are reckoned as nothing.* Aram. כְּלָה. Our Rabbis said (Yoma 20b): The dust of the sun is called לָא i.e., the dust that appears in the sun.

rashi.heb:
*וכמצביה עבד בחיל שמיא.* 
וכרצונו עושה בצבא השמים:
rashi.eng: *and according to His will, He does with the host of heaven.* [as translated,] and according to His will, He does with the host of heaven.

rashi.heb:
*ולא איתי די ימחא בידיה.* 
ולא יש שימחה בידו:
rashi.eng: *and no one can stop His hand.* Aram. בִידֵהּ וְלָא אִיתַי דִּי יְמַחֵא. And there is none who will stop His hand.

notes.243: (tn): The words “feathers” and “claws” are not present in the Aramaic text, but have been added in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ביה זמנא.* 
באותו זמן:
rashi.eng: *At that time.* [as translated,] at that time.

rashi.heb:
*וליקר מלכותי הדרי.* 
ולכבוד מלכותי חזרתי:
rashi.eng: *and I returned to the glory of my kingdom.* [as translated,] and I returned to the glory of my kingdom.

rashi.heb:
*וזיוי.* 
ותואר פני:
rashi.eng: *and my splendor.* the features of my face.

rashi.heb:
*ולי הדברי ורברבני יבעון.* 
ואותי יועצי ושרי היו מבקשים וחפצים שאשוב:
rashi.eng: *my leaders and my dignitaries were seeking me.* and My advisers and my princes were seeking me and hoping for my return.

rashi.heb:
*התקנת.* 
הוכנתי:
rashi.eng: *and I was established.* [as translated,] and I was established.

rashi.heb:
*ורבו יתירה הוספת לי.* 
וגדולה יתירה מן הראשונה נתוספת לי, אמרו רבותינו שרכב על ארי וקשר תנין בראשו:
rashi.eng: *and excessive greatness was added to me.* and more greatness than the earlier [kings] was added to me. Our Rabbis said (Shab. 150a) that he rode astride a lion and tied a serpent to its head.

rashi.heb:
*וארחתה דין.* 
ודרכיו משפט:
rashi.eng: *and Whose ways are just.* His ways are just.

rashi.heb:
*ודי מהלכין בגוה.* 
ואשר מהלכין בגאוה יכול להשפיל:
rashi.eng: *who walk with arrogance.* Those who walk with arrogance He can humble.

notes.246: (tc): The present translation reads כְּלָא (k�la’), with many medieval Hebrew MSS, rather than כְּלָה (k�lah) of BHS.

notes.248: (tc): The translation reads הַדְרֵת (hadret, “I returned”) rather than the MT הַדְרִי (hadri, “my honor”); cf. Theodotion.
notes.249: (tc): The translation reads הָתְקְנֵת (hotq�net, “I was established”) rather than the MT הָתְקְנַת (hotq�nat, “it was established”). As it stands, the MT makes no sense here.

notes.251: (sn): As is clear from the extra-biblical records, it was actually Nabonidus (ca. 556-539 B.C.) who was king of Babylon at this time. However, Nabonidus spent long periods of time at Teima, and during those times Belshazzar his son was de facto king of Babylon. This arrangement may help to explain why later in this chapter Belshazzar promises that the successful interpreter of the handwriting on the wall will be made third ruler in the kingdom. If Belshazzar was in effect second ruler in the kingdom, this would be the highest honor he could grant.
notes.252: (sn): This scene of a Babylonian banquet calls to mind a similar grandiose event recorded in Esth 1:3-8. Persian kings were also renowned in the ancient Near Eastern world for their lavish banquets.
notes.253: (sn): The king probably sat at an elevated head table.

rashi.heb:

rashi.heb:
*עבד לחם רב.* 
עשה סעודה גדולה מצינו בספר יוסיפון שנלחם ביום עם דריוש המדי וכורש ונצח המלחמה ולערב עשה משתה כמו שנבא עליו ישעיה ערוך השלחן צפה הצפית אכול ושתה קומו השרים וגו' שבתוך המשתה חזרו אויביו ונלחמו על העיר ולכדוה:
rashi.eng: *made a great feast.* We find in Josephon (Book 1, ch. 3) that he waged war by day with Darius the Mede and Cyrus and was victorious in the battle. So in the evening he made a feast, as Isaiah had prophesied about him: (21:5) “Setting the table, setting up the lamp, eating, drinking. ‘Arise, princes, etc.’ ” For in the midst of the feast the enemies returned, waged war on the city and captured it.

notes.302: (tc): The Aramaic word is plural. Theodotion has the singular (cf. NAB “PERES”).

notes.303: (tn): Or “word” or “event.” See HALOT 1915 s.v. מִלָּה.
notes.304: (tn): The Aramaic term מְנֵא (m�ne’) is a noun referring to a measure of weight. The linkage here to the verb “to number” (Aram. מְנָה, m�nah) is a case of paronomasia rather than strict etymology. So also with תְּקֵל (t�qel) and פַרְסִין (farsin). In the latter case there is an obvious wordplay with the name “Persian.”

notes.305: (sn): Peres (פְּרֵס) is the singular form of פַרְסִין (pharsin) in v. 25.

rashi.heb:

כלומר ופרסין משמע שני פרסין האחד פריסת מלכותך נשתברה מלכותך והשני שנתנה למדי ופרס:

notes.308: (sn): The year was 539 B.C. At this time Daniel would have been approximately eighty-one years old. The relevant extra-biblical records describing the fall of Babylon include portions of Herodotus, Xenophon, Berossus (cited in Josephus), the Cyrus Cylinder, and the Babylonian Chronicle.

notes.309: (sn): Beginning with , the verse numbers through in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Aramaic text (BHS), with ET = AT, ET = AT, ET = AT, ET = AT, etc., through ET = AT. Beginning with the verse numbers in the English Bible and the Aramaic text are again the same.

notes.311: (tn): This is a technical term for an official placed in charge of a region of the empire (cf. KJV, NLT “prince[s]”; NCV, TEV “governors”). These satraps were answerable to a supervisor, who in turn answered to Darius.

rashi.heb:
*ודריוש: מדאה קבל מלכותא כבר שנין שיתין ותרתין.* 
למה מנה שנותיו לומר לך ביום שנכנס נבוכדנצר להיכל בימי יהויקים (צ"ל יהויכין) נולד שטנו דריוש מגלות יכניה ועד כאן ס"ב שנה ואמר מר גלו בימי יהויכין בשבע לכיבוש יהויקים שהוא שמנה לנבוכדנצר נשתיירו לנבוכדנצר שלשים ושבע שהרי מ"ה מלך ושלשה ועשרים דאויל מרודך כמ"ש רז"ל במסכת מגילה ב' שעבדו לבלשצר הרי ס"ב:
rashi.eng: *And Darius the Mede received the kingdom at the age of sixty-two.* Why does he count his years? To tell you that on the day that Nebuchadnezzar entered the Heichal in the days of Jehoiachin, his adversary, Darius, was born (Seder Olam ch. 28). From the exile of Jeconiah until now were sixty-two years, and the master said: They were exiled in the days of Jehoiachin in the seventh year counting from the conquest of Jehoiakim, which is eight years after the beginning of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign. There remained to Nebuchadnezzar’s reign thirty-seven years, for he reigned forty-five years, and twenty-three of Evil-merodach’s, as our Sages stated in Tractate Megillah (11b), and the two years of Belshazzar that passed, totaling sixty-two.

rashi.heb:
*ועלא מנהון.*

notes.316: (tn): Aram “no negligence or corruption was found in him.” The Greek version of Theodotion lacks the phrase “and no negligence or corruption was found in him.”

rashi.heb:
*דניאל דנה.*

*מתנצח.* 
מתגבר:

*ומלכא עשית.* 
המלך היה חושב בלבו להקימו על כולם:
rashi.eng: *and the king contemplated.* The king was thinking in his heart to set him up over all of them.

rashi.heb:
*הוו בעין עלה.* 
היו מבקשים עלילה למצוא לדניאל בדבר המלכות שיוכלו להלשין עליו:

notes.319: (tn): The Aramaic verb רְגַשׁ (r�gash) occurs three times in this chapter (vv. 7, 12, 16). Its meaning is widely disputed by commentators, and the versions vary considerably in how they render the word. The suggestion that it means “to come thronging” (BDB 1112 s.v.; cf. NAB) seems inappropriate, since it is unlikely that subordinates would enter a royal court in such a reckless fashion. The ancient versions struggled with the word and are not in agreement in their understanding of its meaning. In this chapter the word apparently means to act in agreement with other parties in the pursuit of a duplicitous goal, namely the entrapment of Daniel. Cf. NIV, NCV “went as a group”; NRSV “conspired and came to the king.”

rashi.heb:
*די לא נהשכח.* 
אמרו ביניהם לא נמצא לדניאל זה שום עלילה:
rashi.eng: *No pretext can be found.* They said among themselves, “No pretext can be found about this Daniel.”

rashi.heb:
*להן השכחנא עלוהי.* 
אבל נמצא עליו עלילה ע"י תורת אלהיו אם נוכל לבקש מאת פני המלך שום גזירה שיגזור להעבירו על תורתו והוא לא יקיים את מצות המלך והרי העלילה:
rashi.eng: *but we shall find [a pretext] against him.* but we shall find a pretext against him through the law of his God if we ask the king to issue some decree to cause him to transgress His law, and he will not fulfill the king’s command; and this is the pretext.

rashi.heb:
*הרגישו.* 
משמשו על המלך:
rashi.eng: *assembled.* Aram. הַרְגִּישׁוּ, they approached the king.

notes.322: (tn): Aram “establish a written interdict and inscribe a written decree.”

rashi.heb:
*אתיעטו.* 
נועצו:
rashi.eng: *have taken counsel.* [as translated,] have taken counsel.

rashi.heb:
*לקימה קים מלכא.* 
להחזיק בדת המלך בכח לפי שמחדש באת למלוך וממדינה אחרת אתה וצריך חיזוק:
rashi.eng: *to preserve the king’s law.* to preserve the king’s law with power because you have recently ascended the throne. [Moreover], you are from another country and are in need of support.

rashi.heb:
*די יבעה בעו.* 
אשר יבקש שום בקשה:
rashi.eng: *make any request.* [as translated,] make any request.

rashi.heb:
*להן מנך מלכא.* 
זולתי ממך המלך:
rashi.eng: *except from you, O King.* [as translated,] except from you, O King.

rashi.heb:
*לגוב אריותא.* 
לבור שאריות המלך שם:
rashi.eng: *into a pit of lions.* into the pit where the king’s lions were [kept].

rashi.heb:
*תקים אסרא.* 
תעמיד חק זה:
rashi.eng: *you shall issue a decree.* lit. you shall put up this decree.

rashi.heb:
*די לא להשניה.* 
שלא לשנות כדת מדי ופרס:
rashi.eng: *that will not be amended.* that will not be amended, like the law of Media and Persia.

rashi.heb:
*די לא תעדא.* 
שלא תעבור:
rashi.eng: *which will not be repealed.* which will not pass.

notes.325: (sn): In later rabbinic thought this verse was sometimes cited as a proof text for the notion that one should pray only in a house with windows. See b. Berakhot 34b.
notes.326: (map): For the location of Jerusalem see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.327: (sn): This is apparently the only specific mention in the OT of prayer being regularly offered three times a day. The practice was probably not unique to Daniel, however.
notes.328: (tc): Read with several medieval Hebrew MSS and printed editions הֲוָה (havah) rather than the MT הוּא (hu’).
notes.329: (tn): Aram “kneeling on his knees” (so NASB). No specific posture for offering prayers is prescribed in the OT. Kneeling, as here, and standing were both practiced.

notes.330: (tn): Aram “those men”; the referent (the administrative officials who had earlier approached the king about the edict) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*כדי ידע.* 
וכאשר ידע:
rashi.eng: *when he knew.* and when he found out.

rashi.heb:
*וכוין פתיחין ליה בעליתה.* 
בעלייתו:
rashi.eng: *where there were open windows in his upper chamber.* Aram. בְּעִלִּיתֵהּ, in his upper story.

rashi.heb:
*נגד ירושלם.* 
לצד בה"מ ואע"פ שחרב עשה כמו שאמר שלמה והתפללו אליך דרך ארצם (מלכים א ח):
rashi.eng: *opposite Jerusalem.* toward the side of the Temple, and although it was in ruins, he did as Solomon said (I Kings 8:48): “and pray to You toward their land.”

rashi.heb:
*וזמנין תלתה.* 
ערבית ושחרית ומנחה:
rashi.eng: *and three times.* the evening prayer, the morning prayer and the afternoon prayer.

rashi.heb:
*ברך על ברכוהי.* 
כורע על ברכיו:
rashi.eng: *kneeled on his knees.* [as translated,] kneeled on his knees.

rashi.heb:
*כל קבל די הוא עבד וגו'.* 
ככל אשר היה עושה לפני זאת:
rashi.eng: *as he had done prior to this.* just as all that he had done before this.

notes.331: (tc): The MT also has “about the edict of the king,” but this phrase is absent in the LXX and the Syriac. The present translation deletes the expression. Aram “before the king.”

rashi.heb:
*הרגישו.* 
משמשו ותפשו:
rashi.eng: *searched.* Aram. הַרְגִישּׁוּ, tapped and searched.

notes.333: (tn): Aram “from the sons of the captivity [of].”

rashi.heb:
*על אסר מלכא.* 
על בטול אסור המלך אשר באו להלשין:
rashi.eng: *concerning the king’s decree.* concerning the infraction of the king’s decree, about which they had come to inform.

rashi.heb:
*יציבא מילתא.* 
אמת הדבר:
rashi.eng: *the thing is true.* [as translated,] the thing is true.

rashi.heb:
*לא שם עלך: מלכא טעם.* 
לא נתן לב ועצה לחוש על גזירותיך:
rashi.eng: *did not pay heed to you, O king.* He did not pay heed or counsel to care about your decrees.

rashi.heb:
*בעא בעותיה.* 
מתפלל תפלתו:
rashi.eng: *he offers up his prayer.* Aram. בָּעֵא בָּעוּתֵה, he prays his prayer.

notes.338: (tc): Theodotion lacks the words “came by collusion to the king and.”
notes.340: (tn): Aram “know”; NAB “Keep in mind”; NASB “Recognize”; NIV, NCV “Remember.”

rashi.heb:
*כדי מלתא שמע.* 
כאשר שמע הדבר:
rashi.eng: *when… heard the thing.* [as translated,] when he heard the thing.

rashi.heb:
*שגיא באש עלוהי.* 
הרבה הרע בעיניו שהיה אוהב את דניאל וקשה עליו מיתתו:
rashi.eng: *he became very displeased.* It was very bad in his eyes because he loved Daniel, and his death would be painful to him.

rashi.heb:
*ועל דניאל שם בל לשיזבותיה.* 
על דניאל שם דחוי לדחות הדבר להצילו ואמר להם איני מאמין לכם:
rashi.eng: *and he gave Daniel a reprieve to save him.* He gave Daniel a reprieve to push off the matter to save him, and he said to them, “I don’t believe you.”

rashi.heb:
*בל.* 
איני יודע דוגמתו אך ענינו יורה פתרונו:
rashi.eng: *a reprieve.* Aram. בָּל. I do not know of any word like it, but its context shows its meaning.

rashi.heb:
*ועד מעלי שמשא.* 
ועד בא השמש היה משתדל להצילו אבל כשהגיע זמן תפילתו כרע להקב"ה על ברכיו והתפלל תפלתו ושוב לא היה לו פתחון פה להצילו:
rashi.eng: *and until sunset.* and until sunset he tried to save him, but when the time of his prayer arrived, he prayed his prayer, and the king had no longer had a pretext to save him.

notes.342: (sn): The den was perhaps a pit below ground level which could be safely observed from above.

rashi.heb:
*די מלכא יהקם.* 
אשר המלך יגזור ויעמוד לא לאדם לשנותו:
rashi.eng: *that the king establishes.* What the king decrees and ratifies, no man can alter.

notes.345: (sn): The purpose of the den being sealed was to prevent unauthorized tampering with the opening of the den. Any disturbance of the seal would immediately alert the officials to improper activity of this sort.

notes.347: (tn): The meaning of Aramaic דַּחֲוָה (dakhavah) is a crux interpretum. Suggestions include “music,” “dancing girls,” “concubines,” “table,” “food” – all of which are uncertain. The translation employed here, suggested by earlier scholars, is deliberately vague. A number of recent English versions follow a similar approach with “entertainment” (e.g., NASB, NIV, NCV, TEV, CEV, NLT). On this word see further, HALOT 1849-50 s.v.; E. Vogt, Lexicon linguae aramaicae, 37.

rashi.heb:
*והיתית אבן חדה.* 
והובאת אבן אחת בכל ארץ בבל אין אבן כי אם לבנים כמ"ש הבה נלבנה לבנים (בראשית יא) למדנו שאין אבן בבבל ולפי שעה הביאוה מלאכים מא"י אם התנה במעשה בראשית על הים שיקרע לבני ישראל ועל האש שיצטנן לחנניה וחביריו ועל האריות מהזיק לדניאל לא התנה על זריקת אבן וזיין שלא יזיק באדם והמלך אמר מעם האריות אי אפשר לסלקו שכבר נגזרה גזירה אזדהר בו מהזקת אדם והנס אם יבא יבא סא"א:
rashi.eng: *And a stone was brought.* lit. and one stone was brought. Throughout the entire land of Babylon there are no stones but bricks, as it is written: (Gen 11:3): “Let us make bricks.” We learn that there are no stones in Babylon, but for the occasion, angels brought it [a stone] from the land of Israel. If God stipulated with the Creation on the sea that it should split for the Children of Israel, and on the fire that it cool off for Hananiah and his colleagues, and on the lions that they should not hurt Daniel, He did not stipulate about casting stones or weapons that they should not hurt any man. So the king said, “From the lions I cannot take him away. I shall be careful with him that no man hurt him, and if the miracle comes, let it come.” This does not appear in some editions.

rashi.heb:
*ושמת על פים גובא.* 
הושמה על פי הגומא:
rashi.eng: *and placed on the mouth of the pit.* [as translated,] and placed on the mouth of the pit.

rashi.heb:
*בעזקתיה.* 
בטבעתו שלא יזיזוה ממקומו וישליכו עליו אבנים להרגו:
rashi.eng: *with his signet ring.* with his signet ring so that no one could move it from its place and cast stones upon him to kill him.

rashi.heb:
*די לא תשנא צבו בדניאל.* 
שלא ישתנה רצונו כלומר שלא יעשו לו היזק שלא כרצונו (ס"א כרצונם):
rashi.eng: *that his will about Daniel not be altered.* so that his will should not be changed; i.e., so that they should not harm him against his [the king’s] will.

rashi.heb:
*ובת טות.* 
לן בתענית:
rashi.eng: *and retired while fasting.* [as translated,] and retired while fasting.

rashi.heb:
*ודחון.* 
ושלחן במשנה כך פתר דונש לא הכניסו לפניו שלחן לאכול:
rashi.eng: *table.* Aram. וְּדַּחֲוָן, and a table, in the Mishnah (Tosefta Kelim, B.M. 5:1). So did Dunash explain (p. 58). They did not bring before him a table upon which to eat.

rashi.heb:
*ושנתה נדת עלוהי.* 
נדדה שנתו:
rashi.eng: *and his sleep wandered from him.* [as translated,] his sleep wandered.

notes.349: (tn): Aram “The king answered and said to Daniel.” This phrase has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons; it is redundant in English.

rashi.heb:
*בשפרפרא.* 
בעלות שחר והרבה יש בתרגום יונתן:
rashi.eng: *at dawn.* Aram. בִּשְׁפַרְפָרָה, at the rise of dawn, and there are many [examples of this] in Targum Jonathan.

rashi.heb:
*יקום בנגהא.* 
עמד לאור הבוקר ולא בשלש שעות כשאר מלכים:
rashi.eng: *arose to the light of morning.* He arose at the light of morning, not after three hours, like other kings.

rashi.heb:
*ובהתבהלה לגובא די אריותא אזל.* 
ובבהלה לחפירת האריות אזל:
rashi.eng: *and in haste went to the pit of the lions.* [as translated,] and in haste went to the pit of the lions.

rashi.heb:
*חבולה לא עבדת.* 
שום דבר כיעור ושקר לא עשיתי:
rashi.eng: *I have done no harm.* No unseemly or false act have I committed.

notes.352: (tn): Aram “had eaten the pieces of.” The Aramaic expression is ironic, in that the accusers who had figuratively “eaten the pieces of Daniel” are themselves literally devoured by the lions.
notes.353: (tn): The Aramaic active impersonal verb is often used as a substitute for the passive.
notes.354: (tc): The LXX specifies only the two overseers, together with their families, as those who were cast into the lions’ den.

rashi.heb:
*שגיא טאב עלוהי.* 
הרבה הוטב בעיניו:
rashi.eng: *it pleased… exceedingly.* It was very good in his eyes.

rashi.heb:
*ולדניאל.* 
ואת דניאל צוה להעלות מן הבור:
rashi.eng: *and… Daniel.* and he ordered that Daniel be lifted up out of the pit.

rashi.heb:
*די הימן באלהיה.* 
אשר האמין באלהיו:
rashi.eng: *because he believed in his God.* [as translated,] because he believed in his God.

rashi.heb:
*די אכלו קרצוהי.* 
אשר הלשינו עליו:
rashi.eng: *who had informed on Daniel.* [as translated,] who had informed on Daniel.

rashi.heb:
*ולא מטו לארעית גובא.* 
לא הגיעו לתחתיות הבור עד שמשלו בהם האריות וכל עצמותיהם הדיקו:
rashi.eng: *and they did not reach the bottom of the pit.* They did not reach the bottom of the pit before the lions overwhelmed them and crushed their bones to powder.

rashi.heb:
*באדין דריוש מלכא וכו'.* 
די דארין בכל ארעא שדרין בכל הארץ שלמכון יסגא:
rashi.eng: *Then King Darius… that lived in all the land, May your peace increase!.* [as translated,] that lived in all the land, May your peace increase!

notes.358: (tn): Or perhaps “in the reign of Darius, even in the reign of Cyrus.” The identity of this Darius is disputed. Some take the name to be referring to Cyrus, understanding the following vav (ו, “and”) in an epexegetical sense (“even”). Others identify Darius with a governor of Babylon known from extra-biblical records as Gubaru, or with Cambyses, son of Cyrus. Many scholars maintain that the reference is historically inaccurate.

rashi.heb:
*ובמלכות כורש.* 
שמלך אחר דריוש שלא מלך דריוש המדי אלא שנה אחת ונהרג במלחמה כאשר כתוב בספר יוסף בן גוריון והמליכו את כורש חתנו עליהם בתוך החיל:
rashi.eng: *and in the kingdom of Cyrus.* who reigned after Darius, for Darius reigned only one year, and he was slain in battle, as it is written in the book of Joseph ben Gurion, and they crowned Cyrus his son-in-law in the midst of the battle.

notes.359: (sn): The first year of Belshazzar’s reign would have been ca. 553 B.C. Daniel would have been approximately 67 years old at the time of this vision.
notes.361: (tn): Aram “and visions of his head.” The Aramaic is difficult here. Some scholars add a verb thought to be missing (e.g., “the visions of his head [were alarming him]”), but there is no external evidence to support such a decision and the awkwardness of the text at this point may be original.
notes.362: (tn): Aram “head of words.” The phrase is absent in Theodotion. Cf. NIV “the substance of his dream.”

rashi.heb:
*באדין חלמא כתב.* 
אז (החלום כתב) וראשי הדברים אמר:
rashi.eng: *then he wrote the dream.* Then [he wrote the dream] and told the beginnings of the matters.

notes.365: (tn): Or “the heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heavens” or “sky” depending on the context.
notes.366: (sn): The referent of the great sea is unclear. The common view that the expression refers to the Mediterranean Sea is conjectural.

rashi.heb:
*וארו.* 
והנה:
rashi.eng: *and behold.* [as translated,] and behold.

rashi.heb:
*ארבע רוחי שמיא מגיחין וגו'.* 
ד' רוחות נושבות באות מד' רוחות העולם ונלחמות עם הים הגדול וסוערות אותו:
rashi.eng: *the four winds of the heavens were stirring up, etc..* four blowing winds coming from the four directions of the world and waging war with the Great Sea and stirring it up.

rashi.heb:
*וארבע חיון.* 
וד' חיות:
rashi.eng: *And four beasts.* [as translated,] and four beasts.

rashi.heb:
*שנין דא מן דא.* 
משונות זו מזו:
rashi.eng: *each one different from the other.* [as translated,] each one different from the other.

notes.368: (sn): The identity of the first animal, derived from v. 17 and the parallels in chap. 2, is Babylon. The reference to the plucking of its wings is probably a reference to the time of Nebuchadnezzar’s insanity (cf. chap. 4). The latter part of v. 4 then describes the restoration of Nebuchadnezzar. The other animals have traditionally been understood to represent respectively Media-Persia, Greece, and Rome, although most of modern scholarship identifies them as Media, Persia, and Greece. For a biblical parallel to the mention of lion, bear, and leopard together, see Hos 13:7-8.

rashi.heb:
*קדמיתא כאריה וגפין די נשר לה.* 
היא כאריה ולה כנפי נשר זו היא מלכות בבל שהיתה מושלת באותה שעה וכך ראה אותה ירמיה שנאמר עלה אריה מסבכו (ירמיהו ה׳:ו׳) ואומר הנה כאשר ידאה וגו' (שם מח):
rashi.eng: *The first one was like a lion, and it had the wings of an eagle.* It was like a lion, and it had the wings of an eagle; that is the kingdom of Babylon, which was ruling at that time, and so did Jeremiah see it (4:7): “A lion has come up from its thicket,” and he says also (48:40): “like an eagle he shall soar.”

rashi.heb:
*עד די מריטו גפה.* 
נמרטו כנפיה זו היא רמז למפלתה:
rashi.eng: *until its wings were plucked.* Its wings were plucked, which is an allusion to its downfall

rashi.heb:
*ונטילת מן ארעא.* 
ל' נסתלק מן הארץ רמז שתבטל המלכות מן הארץ:
rashi.eng: *and it was taken from the earth.* an expression of being removed from the earth, an allusion to the curtailment of the kingdom from the world.

rashi.heb:
*ולבב אנש.* 
ל' חלשות כמו ידעו הגוים אנוש המה סלה:
rashi.eng: *and the heart of a mortal.* Aram. וּלְבַב אֶנָשׁ, an expression of weakness, like (Psalms 9:21): “Let the nations know that they are forever mortal men (אֶנוֹשׁ)”.

notes.370: (sn): The three ribs held securely in the mouth of the bear, perhaps representing Media-Persia, apparently symbolize military conquest, but the exact identity of the “ribs” is not clear. Possibly it is a reference to the Persian conquest of Lydia, Egypt, and Babylonia.
notes.371: (tc): The LXX lacks the phrase “between its teeth.”
notes.372: (tn): Aram “and thus they were saying to it.”

rashi.heb:
*אחרי.* 
אחרת:
rashi.eng: *another.* [as translated,] another.

rashi.heb:
*תנינה.* 
שעלתה שניה מן הים:
rashi.eng: *second.* that emerged second from the sea.

rashi.heb:
*דמיה לדוב.* 
זה רמז למלכות פרס שתמלך אחר בבל שאוכלים ושותים כדוב ומסורבלים בבשר כדוב:
rashi.eng: *resembling a bear.* This represents the kingdom of Persia, which will reign after Babylon, who eats and drinks like a bear and is enwrapped in flesh like a bear.

rashi.heb:
*דמיה לדוב.* 
לדב כתיב כמו דיבא תרגום של זאב שאף זאב נקראת מלכות פרס שנא' ע"כ הכם אריה מיער זאב ערבות ישדדם:
rashi.eng: *resembling a bear.* It is spelled לְדֹב [without a “vav,”] like דִיבָא, the Aramaic for זְאֵב, a wolf, for the kingdom of Persia was also called a wolf, as it is said: (Jer. 5:6): “Therefore a lion smote them, a wolf of the deserts spoils them.”

rashi.heb:
*ולשטר חד הקימת.* 
ולצד א' עמדה רמז לשיפסוק מלכות בבל תמתין פרס שנה אחת שתמלך מדי:
rashi.eng: *and it stood to one side.* and it stood to one side, indicating that when the kingdom of Babylon terminates, Persia will wait one year, when Media will reign.

rashi.heb:
*ותלת עלעין בפומיה.* 
שלש צלעות רבותינו פירשו ג' מדינות היו תמיד מורדות בה ומשלימות עמה פעמים בולעתן ופעמים פולטתן זהו בפומה בין שניה פעמים חוץ לשניה פעמים לתוכן ואני אומר תלת עלעין שלשה מלכים שיעמדו לפרס כורש ואחשורוש ודריוש שבנה הבית:
rashi.eng: *and there were three ribs in its mouth.* Aram. וּתְלָת עִלָעִין בְּפֻמַּהּ, three ribs. Our Sages explained that three provinces were constantly rebelling against it [i.e., Persia] and making peace with it; sometimes it would swallow them and sometimes spit them out. That is the meaning of “in its mouth between its teeth,” sometimes outside its teeth, sometimes inside (Kid. 72a), but I say that the three עִלָעִין are three kings who will rise from Persia: Cyrus, Ahasuerus, and Darius who built the Temple.

rashi.heb:
*בשר שגיא.* 
בשר הרבה:
rashi.eng: *much meat.* [as translated,] much meat.

notes.376: (sn): If the third animal is Greece, the most likely identification of these four heads is the four-fold division of the empire of Alexander the Great following his death. See note on Dan 8:8.

rashi.heb:
*גפין ארבע וגו'.* 
וארבעה ראשין הם ד' מושלים שחלק להם אלכסנדרוס מוקדון במותו את מלכותו כמו שכתוב בספר יוסף בן גוריון שהחיה הזאת השלישית היא מלכות אנטיוכוס ונקרא נמר על שם שהיתה גוזרת גזרות על ישראל מנומרות ומשונות זו מזו:
rashi.eng: *four wings… four heads.* They are the four rulers to whom Alexander of Macedon allotted his kingdom at his death, as is written in the book of Joseph ben Gurion (Book 3, ch. 14), for this third beast is the kingdom of Antiochus, and it is called נָמֵר because it issued decrees upon Israel [which were] spotted (מְנֻמָּרוֹת) and varied one from the other.

rashi.heb:
*ושלטן יהב לה.* 
וממשלה נתנה לה:
rashi.eng: *and dominion was given it.* [as translated,] and dominion was given it.

notes.377: (tn): The Aramaic text has also “and behold.” So also in vv. 8, 13.
notes.378: (sn): The fourth animal differs from the others in that it is nondescript. Apparently it was so fearsome that Daniel could find nothing with which to compare it. Attempts to identify this animal as an elephant or other known creature are conjectural.
notes.379: (tn): The Aramaic word for “teeth” is dual rather than plural, suggesting two rows of teeth.

rashi.heb:
*בחזוי ליליא.* 
בלילה אחרת, השלש הראשונות ראה בלילה אחת, וזו בלילה אחרת על שם שהיא שקולה כנגד שלשתן בויקרא רבה:
rashi.eng: *in the visions of the night.* on another night. The first three he saw on one night, and this one on another night, because it is equal to them all. In Leviticus Rabbah (13:5).

rashi.heb:
*ושנין די פרזל לה.* 
שיני ברזל לה:
rashi.eng: *and it had… iron teeth.* [as translated,] iron teeth.

rashi.heb:
*ומדקה.* 
מדיקה ושוחקת הדק:
rashi.eng: *and crushed.* It crushed and ground finely.

rashi.heb:
*ושארא.* 
מותר אכילתה:
rashi.eng: *and… the rest.* what it left over from its eating.

rashi.heb:
*וקרנין עשר.* 
עשר קרנות זו פי' לו המלאך שהם עשרה מלכים שיעמדו לרומי קודם לאספסיינוס שחרב את הבית:
rashi.eng: *and… ten horns.* Aram. וְקַרְנַיִן עֲשַׂר. The angel explained to him that these are the ten kings who would ascend [the throne] of Rome before Vespasian, who would destroy the Temple.

rashi.heb:
*ואלו.* 
כמו וארו לשון הנה:
rashi.eng: *and behold.* Aram. וַאֲלוּ, like וַאֲרוּ, an expression of “behold.”

rashi.heb:
*ממלל רברבן.* 
דברי גאוה, הוא טיטוס שאחז"ל שחרף וגדף ונכנס להיכל בעזות פנים:
rashi.eng: *speaking arrogantly.* words of arrogance. That is Titus, about whom the Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Gittin 56b) that he blasphemed and berated and entered the Heichal with brazenness.

notes.382: (tn): Or “the Ancient One” (NAB, NRSV, NLT), although the traditional expression has been retained in the present translation because it is familiar to many readers. Cf. TEV “One who had been living for ever”; CEV “the Eternal God.”
notes.383: (tn): Traditionally the Aramaic word נְקֵא (n�qe’) has been rendered “pure,” but here it more likely means “of a lamb.” Cf. the Syriac neqya’ (“a sheep, ewe”). On this word see further, M. Sokoloff, “’amar neqe’, ‘Lamb’s Wool’ (Dan 7:9),” JBL 95 (1976): 277-79.

rashi.heb:
*די כרסון רמיו.* 
כסאות הוטלו ונתקנו לישב במשפט אחד לדין וא' לצדקה לישראל:
rashi.eng: *until thrones were set up.* Thrones were set up and established to sit in judgment, one for judgment for the nations of the world and one for charity for Israel.

rashi.heb:
*ועתיק יומין יתיב.* 
הקב"ה יושב למשפט על המלכות הזו ועל שלפניה שהכעיסו לפניו והציקו לבניו:
rashi.eng: *and the Ancient of Days sat.* The Holy One, blessed be He, was sitting in judgment on this kingdom and on those before it, who provoked Him and oppressed His children.

rashi.heb:
*כתלג חיור.* 
ללבן עונות עמו:
rashi.eng: *as white as snow.* to whiten the iniquities of His people.

rashi.heb:
*ושער ראשה כעמר נקא.* 
מנקה עצמו מזכיות שיש לעכו"ם לפניו ומשלם להם כל שכרם בעולם הזה בויקרא רבה:
rashi.eng: *and the hair of His head was like clean wool.* He cleanses Himself of the merits that the nations have before Him, and He pays them all their reward in this world. In Lev. Rabbah.

rashi.heb:
*די נור.* 
של אש:
rashi.eng: *of fire.* [as translated,] of fire.

rashi.heb:
*נור דלק.* 
אש בוערה:
rashi.eng: *a burning fire.* [as translated,] a burning fire.

rashi.heb:
*נגד ונפק.* 
מושך ויצא:
rashi.eng: *was flowing and emerging.* [as translated,] was flowing and emerging.

rashi.heb:
*ישמשוניה.* 
לעתיק יומין:
rashi.eng: *serve Him.* i.e., the Ancient of Days.

rashi.heb:
*דינא יתיב.* 
המשפט נתישב לפניו:
rashi.eng: *justice was established.* The judgment is established before Him.

rashi.heb:
*וספרין פתיחו.* 
הספרים נפתחו ספרי העבירות והרעות שעשו:
rashi.eng: *and the books were opened.* The books were opened; the book of the transgressions and the evils that they committed.

notes.387: (tc): The LXX and Theodotion lack the words “I was watching” here. It is possible that these words in the MT are a dittography from the first part of the verse.

rashi.heb:
*מן קל מליא.* 
מקול הדברים הגבוהים שהקרן מדברת עלתה חמתו של עתיק יומין:
rashi.eng: *from the sound of the arrogant words.* From the sound of the haughty words that the horn was speaking, the wrath of the Ancient of Days was aroused.

rashi.heb:
*עד דקטלת חיותא והובד גשמה.* 
אבד גופה:
rashi.eng: *until the beast was slain and its body was destroyed and given.* [as translated,] and its body was destroyed.

rashi.heb:
*ליקדת אשא.* 
ללבת אש הוא אשו של יעקב והיה בית יעקב אש וגו' (עובדיה א׳:י״ח):
rashi.eng: *to a flame of fire.* to a flame of fire; this refers to Jacob’s fire etc.

notes.389: (tn): Aram “a prolonging of life was granted to them.”

rashi.heb:
*ושאר חיותא העדיו שלטנהון.* 
ולשאר המלכיות הסירו מן השמים ממשלתהון:
rashi.eng: *But as for the other beasts, their dominion was removed.* And from the other kingdoms, their dominion was removed by Heaven.

rashi.heb:
*וארכה בחיין יהיבת להון.* 
וזמן נתן להם בחיים עד יום מועד לעתיד לבא מלחמות גוג ומגוג:
rashi.eng: *and they were given an extension of life.* And He gave them time to live until a set day in the future, the wars of Gog and Magog.

rashi.heb:
*ארכה.* 
המתנה:
rashi.eng: *an extension.* Aram. אַרְכָה, waiting.

notes.390: (tc): The LXX has ἐπί (epi, “upon”) here (cf. Matt 24:30; 26:64). Theodotion has μετά (meta, “with”) here (cf. Mark 14:62; Rev 1:7).
notes.391: (tn): Or “the heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heavens” or “sky” depending on the context.
notes.392: (sn): This text is probably the main OT background for Jesus’ use of the term “son of man.” In both Jewish and Christian circles the reference in the book of Daniel has traditionally been understood to refer to an individual, usually in a messianic sense. Many modern scholars, however, understand the reference to have a corporate identity. In this view, the “son of man” is to be equated with the “holy ones” (vv. 18, 21, 22, 25) or the “people of the holy ones” (v. 27) and understood as a reference to the Jewish people. Others understand Daniel’s reference to be to the angel Michael.

rashi.heb:
*כבר אנש אתה.* 
הוא מלך המשיח:
rashi.eng: *one like a man was coming.* That is the King Messiah.

rashi.heb:
*ועד עתיק יומיא.* 
שהיה יושב במשפט ודן את האומות:
rashi.eng: *and… up to the Ancient of Days.* Who was sitting in judgment and judging the nations.

rashi.heb:
*מטה.* 
הגיע:
rashi.eng: *came.* arrived, reached.

notes.394: (tn): Some take “serving” here in the sense of “worshiping.”
notes.395: (tn): Aram “is an eternal authority which will not pass away.”
notes.396: (tn): Aram “is one which will not be destroyed.”

rashi.heb:
*וליה יהיב שלטן.* 
ולאותו בן אדם נתן ממשלת האומות דימה כחיות וישראל דימה כבן אדם על שהם ענותנים ותמימים:
rashi.eng: *And He gave him dominion.* And to that man He gave dominion over the nations, for the heathens he likens to beasts, and Israel he likens to a man because they are humble and innocent.

rashi.heb:
*די לא יעדה.* 
לא יסור:
rashi.eng: *which will not be removed.* [as translated,] will not be removed.

notes.397: (tn): The Aramaic text includes the phrase “in its sheath,” apparently viewing the body as a container or receptacle for the spirit somewhat like a sheath or scabbard is for a knife or a sword (cf. NAB “within its sheath of flesh”). For this phrase the LXX and Vulgate have “in these things.”

rashi.heb:
*אתכרית רוחי.* 
לשון כי יכרה (שמות כב) ולשון ארמי ועברי שוין בו כלומר נסחה מתוך עומק כרייתה:
rashi.eng: *My spirit… became troubled.* Aram. אֶתְכְּרִיַת an expression of (Exod. 21:33): “or if… digs (יִכְרֶה),” and Hebrew and Aramaic are alike in this case; i.e., it was humbled because of the depth of its digging.

rashi.heb:
*בגו נדנה.* 
בתוך תיקה נרתק שלו כלומר נבהלה רוחי בתוך הגוף מן החלום הזה:
rashi.eng: *within its sheath.* Aram. בְּגוֹנִדְנֶה; i.e., my spirit became terrified in my body from this dream.

notes.401: (tn): Aram “matter,” but the matter at hand is of course the vision.

rashi.heb:
*קרבת על חד מן קאמיא.* 
קרבתי אצל א' מן העומדים שם לפני עתיק הימים המלאכים נקראו עומדים שנא' (זכריה ג׳:ז׳) בין העומדים האלה מפני שאין להם קפצים:
rashi.eng: *I drew near to one of those standing.* I drew near to one of those standing there beside the Ancient of Days. The angels are called standing ones, as it is said: (Zech. 3:7): “among these who stand by (הָעמְדִים),” because they have no joints.

rashi.heb:
*ויציבא אבעא מנה.* 
והאמת שאלתי ממנו:
rashi.eng: *and I asked him the truth.* [as translated,] and I asked him the truth.

rashi.heb:
*ארבעה מלכין.* 
ד' מלכיות:
rashi.eng: *four kingdoms.* Aram. אַרְבְּעָא מַלְכִין, lit. four kings.

notes.402: (sn): The expression holy ones is either a reference to angels or to human beings devoted to God.

rashi.heb:
*ויקבלון מלכותא קדישי עליונין.* 
אלו ישראל שיטלו המלכות מהרביעית:
rashi.eng: *And the high holy ones will receive the kingdom.* These are Israel, who will take the kingdom from the fourth one.

rashi.heb:
*אדין צבית ליצבא.* 
אז חפצתי לעמוד על האמת מן החיה הרביעית:
rashi.eng: *Then I wished to determine the truth.* Then I wished to determine the truth concerning the fourth beast.

rashi.heb:
*די הות שניה מן.* 
כולהון דחילה יתירה אשר היתה משונה מכולן באימה יתירה:
rashi.eng: *which was different from all of them-excessively dreadful.* which was different from all of them with excessive dreadfulness.

notes.404: (tn): The words “I also wanted to know” are added in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.405: (tc): The conjunction in the MT before “eyes” is odd. The ancient versions do not seem to presuppose it.

rashi.heb:
*ונפלה מן.* 
קדמה תלת ונפלו מפניה שלש מן הראשונו':
rashi.eng: *and [the] three [that] fell before it.* and three of the first ones fell before it.

rashi.heb:
*וקרנא דכן ועינין לה.* 
והקרן אשר כזאת ועינים לה ככתוב למעלה:
rashi.eng: *and the horn that was like this and that had eyes.* and the horn that was like this, and had eyes, as is written above.

notes.407: (tn): Aram “prevailing against” (KJV and ASV both similar); NASB “overpowering them”; TEV “conquered them.”

rashi.heb:
*חזה הוית.* 
בחלומי הראשון שספרתי למעלה:
rashi.eng: *I looked.* in my first dream, which I told above.

rashi.heb:
*עם קדישין.* 
עם ישראל:
rashi.eng: *with the holy ones.* with Israel.

notes.408: (tc): In the LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate the verb is active, understanding “judgment” to be the object rather than the subject of the verb (i.e., “the Ancient of Days rendered judgment”). This presupposes a different vocalization of the verb ( יְהַב [y�hav] rather than the MT יְהִב [y�hiv]).

rashi.heb:
*ודינא יהיב לקדישי עליונין.* 
ונקמה נתן להם ממנה:
rashi.eng: *and gave revenge to the high holy ones.* and He gave them revenge from it.

rashi.heb:
*כן אמר.* 
כה ענני המלאך הפותר לי את החלום:
rashi.eng: *So he said.* So did the angel who interpreted the dream for me reply to me.

notes.410: (tn): Or “subjugate”; KJV, NASB, NIV “subdue”; ASV, NRSV “put down.”

rashi.heb:
*וקרניא עשר.* 
וקרנים י' אשר ראיתי לה זה פתרונו:
rashi.eng: *And the ten horns.* And its ten horns that you saw-this is its interpretation.

rashi.heb:
*מנה מלכותא.* 
מאותה המלכות:
rashi.eng: *from that kingdom.* [as translated,] from that kingdom.

rashi.heb:
*ואחרין יקום אחריהון.* 
והאחרון יקום אחריהן הוא טיטוס:
rashi.eng: *and the last one will rise after them.* and the last one will rise after them-that is Titus.

notes.411: (tn): Aram “wear out” (so KJV, ASV, NRSV); NASB, NLT “wear down.” The word is a hapax legomenon in biblical Aramaic, but in biblical Hebrew it especially refers to wearing out such things as garments. Here it is translated “harass…continually.”
notes.413: (tn): Aram “times and law.” The present translation is based on the understanding that the expression is a hendiadys.
notes.414: (sn): Although the word times is vocalized in the MT as a plural, it probably should be regarded as a dual. The Masoretes may have been influenced here by the fact that in late Aramaic (and Syriac) the dual forms fall out of use. The meaning would thus be three and a half “times.”

rashi.heb:
*לצד עלאה.* 
כלפי מעלה:
rashi.eng: *against the Most High.* [as translated,] against the Most High.

rashi.heb:
*ולקדישי עליונין יבלא.* 
ולישראל יטריח ויציק:
rashi.eng: *and he will oppress the high holy ones.* He will burden and oppress Israel.

rashi.heb:
*ויסבר להשניא זמנין ודת.* 
ידמה בלבו להעבירם על כל מועדיהם ודתיהם:
rashi.eng: *and he will think to change the times and the law.* He will plan in his heart to cause them to transgress all their appointed times and their laws.

rashi.heb:
*עד עידן ועידנין ופלג עידן.* 
קץ סתום הוא זה כאשר נאמר לדניאל סתום הדברים וחתום ודרשוהו הראשונים איש לפי דעתו וכלו הקצים ויש לנו לפותרו עוד כאשר ראיתי כתוב בשם רב סעדיה הם אלף וג' מאות ול"ה שנים האמור בסוף הספר אשרי המחכה וגו' ופי' המועד עד עת שני עתים וחצי עת ואמר שהעתים הם ד' מאות ופ' שמיום צאתם ממצרים עד שנבנה הבית, וד' מאות ועשר ימי מקדש ראשון הרי תת"ץ ועוד חצי העת הזה תמ"ה הרי אל"ף של"ה את אלה חשוב מעת הוסר התמיד עד שוב זבח התמיד אל מקומו והוא הוסר שש שנים לפני החורבן ויש קצת ראיה בספר זה, ועוד יש מביאין ראיה לחשבון זה הסתר אסתיר פני הסתר אסתיר בגי' אלף ושל"ה:
rashi.eng: *until a time, two times, and half a time.* This is an obscure end, as was said to Daniel (12:4): “And you, Daniel, close up the words and seal,” and the early commentators expounded on it, each one according to his view, and the ends have passed. We can still interpret it as I saw written in the name of Rav Saadia Gaon, that they are the 1,335 years stated at the end of the Book (12:12): “Fortunate is he who waits [and reaches the days one thousand three hundred and thirty-five],” and he explains the appointed time as until the time of two times and a half time, and he [Rav Saadia Gaon] said that the times are 480 [years], which is the time from the Exodus from Egypt until the Temple was built, and 410 [years], [which are] the days of the First Temple, totaling 890, and another half of this time, 445, totaling 1,335. Figure these from the time the daily sacrifice was discontinued until the daily sacrifice will be restored to its place; it was discontinued six years prior to the destruction, and there is somewhat of a proof in this Book. [See Rashi to 8:14.] Others bring further proof to this computation, namely that (Deut. 31: 18): “And I, will hide My face” [the words] הַסְתֵּר אַסְתִּיר add up in gematria to 1,335.

rashi.heb:
*ודינא יתב.* 
והדין נתישב לפני המקום:
rashi.eng: *And the judgment was established.* And the judgment was established before Him.

rashi.heb:
*ושלטנה יהעדון.* 
ושולטנו וממשלת של אותו המלכות יסירו מן השמים:
rashi.eng: *and they will remove his dominion.* from heaven. They will remove the dominion and the rule of that kingdom.

notes.416: (tn): If the “holy ones” are angels, then this probably refers to the angels as protectors of God’s people. If the “holy ones” are God’s people, then this is an appositional construction, “the people who are the holy ones.” See 8:24 for the corresponding Hebrew phrase and the note there.

rashi.heb:
*וישתמעון.* 
יהיו נשמעים למצותו לעשותו:
rashi.eng: *and obey.* They will obey his command to execute it.

notes.417: (tn): Aram “my brightness was changing on me.”

rashi.heb:
*עד כה.* 
עד כאן:
rashi.eng: *until here.* [as translated,] until here.

rashi.heb:
*שגיא רעיוני יבהלונני.* 
הרבה היו מחשבותי מבהלות אותי:
rashi.eng: *my thoughts terrified me greatly.* My thoughts were terrifying me greatly.

rashi.heb:
*וזיוי ישתנון.* 
מראית יופי ותארי נשתנו:
rashi.eng: *and my colors changed.* The appearance of my good looks and my features changed.

rashi.heb:
*בלבי נטרת.* 
בלבי צפנתי:
rashi.eng: *I kept… in my heart.* I hid in my heart.

notes.419: (sn): Dan 8:1 marks the switch from Aramaic (= 2:4b-7:28) back to Hebrew as the language in which the book is written in its present form. The remainder of the book from this point on (8:1-12:13) is in Hebrew. The bilingual nature of the book has been variously explained, but it most likely has to do with the book’s transmission history.
notes.420: (sn): The third year of King Belshazzar’s reign would have been ca. 551 B.C. Daniel would have been approximately 69 years old at the time of this vision.
notes.421: (tn, Heb): “in the beginning.” This refers to the vision described in chapter seven.

rashi.heb:
*בשנת שלש.* 
אחרי המראה הראשון אחר שנראה אלי בתחילה החלום האמור למעלה שנראה לו בשנת אחד לבלשצר:
rashi.eng: *In the third year.* after the first vision that appeared to me in the beginning, i.e., the dream stated above (7:1), which appeared to him in the first year of Belshazzar.

notes.423: (sn): Susa (Heb. שׁוּשַׁן, shushan), located some 230 miles (380 km) east of Babylon, was a winter residence for Persian kings during the Achaemenid period. The language of v. 2 seems to suggest that Daniel may not have been physically present at Susa, but only saw himself there in the vision. However, the Hebrew is difficult, and some have concluded that the first four words of v. 2 in the MT are a later addition (cf. Theodotion).
notes.424: (tn): The Hebrew word בִּירָה (birah, “castle, palace”) usually refers to a fortified structure within a city, but here it is in apposition to the city name Susa and therefore has a broader reference to the entire city (against this view, however, see BDB 108 s.v. 2). Cf. NAB “the fortress of Susa”; TEV “the walled city of Susa.”
notes.425: (tn): The term אוּבַל (’uval = “stream, river”) is a relatively rare word in biblical Hebrew, found only here and in vv. 3 and 6. The Ulai was apparently a sizable artificial canal in Susa (cf. NASB, NIV, NCV), and not a river in the ordinary sense of that word.

rashi.heb:
*על אובל אולי.* 
על הנהר ששמו אולי:
rashi.eng: *beside the river Ulai.* beside the river named Ulai.

notes.428: (tn, Heb): “one.” The Hebrew numerical adjective occasionally functions like an English indefinite article. See GKC 401 �125.b.

rashi.heb:
*ולו קרנים.* 
רמז למלכות פרס ומדי:
rashi.eng: *and it had horns.* symbolizing the kingdom of Persia and Media.

rashi.heb:
*והאחת גבוהה מן השנית.* 
רמז למלכות פרס שגדולה ממלכות מדי שמלכות מדי לא היתה אלא שנה אחת שנא' (לקמן ט') בשנת אחת לדריוש בן אחשורוש מזרע מדי, ושנינו בסדר עולם לא מצינו שנה למדי בכתובים אלא זו בלבד:
rashi.eng: *and one was higher than the other.* symbolizing the kingdom of Persia, which was greater than the kingdom of Media, for the kingdom of Media existed for only one year, as it says (9:1): “In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus of the seed of Media,” and we learned in Seder Olam (ch. 28): “We do not find any year ascribed to Media in the Holy Writ but this one only.”

rashi.heb:
*והגבוהה עולה באחרונה.* 
רמז הוא שתקדים מלכות מדי למלכות פרס:
rashi.eng: *and the higher one sprouted last.* This symbolizes that the kingdom of Media will precede the kingdom of Persia.

notes.432: (tn): In the Hiphil the Hebrew verb גָּדַל (gadal, “to make great; to magnify”) can have either a positive or a negative sense. For the former, used especially of God, see Ps 126:2, 3; Joel 2:21. In this chapter (8:4, 8, 11, 25) the word has a pejorative sense, describing the self-glorification of this king. The sense seems to be that of vainly assuming one’s own superiority through deliberate hubris.

notes.433: (tn): The words “all this” are added in the translation for stylistic reasons and for clarification.
notes.434: (tn, Heb): “and behold, a he-goat of the goats.”
notes.435: (tn): Or “of the whole earth” (NAB, ASV, NASB, NRSV).
notes.436: (tn, Heb): “a horn of vision” [or “conspicuousness”], i.e., “a conspicuous horn,” one easily seen.

rashi.heb:
*הייתי מבין.* 
הייתי מסתכל בו:
rashi.eng: *I was pondering.* I was contemplating it.

rashi.heb:
*צפיר.* 
שעיר:
rashi.eng: *a he goat.* Heb. צְפִיר.

rashi.heb:
*ואין נוגע בארץ.* 
דומה היה כמדלג באויר:
rashi.eng: *and it did not touch the ground.* He resembled one skipping in the air.

rashi.heb:
*קרן חזות.* 
קרן גדול למראה העין:
rashi.eng: *a conspicuous horn.* Heb. קֶרֶן חָזוּת, a large horn visible to the eye.

notes.441: (tn, Heb): “he hurled him.” The referents of both pronouns (the male goat and the ram) have been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.442: (sn): The goat of Daniel’s vision represents Greece; the large horn represents Alexander the Great. The ram stands for Media-Persia. Alexander’s rapid conquest of the Persians involved three battles of major significance which he won against overwhelming odds: Granicus (334 B.C.), Isus (333 B.C.), and Gaugemela (331 B.C.).

rashi.heb:
*ויתמרמר אליו.* 
וילחם אליו הוא לשון כעס מר:
rashi.eng: *and it fought with it.* Heb. וַיִתְמַרְמַר אֵלָיו, and it fought with it. That is an expression of bitter (מַר) anger.

notes.443: (tn): The word “horns” is not in the Hebrew text, but is implied.
notes.444: (sn): The four conspicuous horns refer to Alexander’s successors. After his death, Alexander’s empire was divided up among four of his generals: Cassander, who took Macedonia and Greece; Lysimachus, who took Thrace and parts of Asia Minor; Seleucus, who took Syria and territory to its east; and Ptolemy, who took control of Egypt.
notes.445: (tn): Or “the heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heavens” or “sky” depending on the context.

rashi.heb:
*חזות ארבע.* 
מראה ארבע קרנים:
rashi.eng: *an appearance of four.* an appearance of four horns.

notes.446: (sn): This small horn is Antiochus IV Epiphanes, who controlled the Seleucid kingdom from ca. 175-164 B.C. Antiochus was extremely hostile toward the Jews and persecuted them mercilessly.
notes.447: (sn): The expression the beautiful land (Heb. הַצֶּבִי [hats�vi] = “the beauty”) is a cryptic reference to the land of Israel. Cf. 11:16, 41, where it is preceded by the word אֶרֶץ (’erets, “land”).

rashi.heb:
*ומן האחת מהם.* 
ומאחת מאלו המלכיות:
rashi.eng: *And from one of them.* and from one of these kingdoms.

rashi.heb:
*יצא קרן אחת.* 
מלכות טיטוס יוצאת ממנו:
rashi.eng: *emerged a… horn.* The kingdom of Titus emerged from it.

rashi.heb:
*מצעירה.* 
מלכות מוצערת ונבזית כמו שקראו למעלה קרן אחת מצעירה. והוא על ענין שנא' בזוי אתה מאד (עובדיה א׳:ב׳):
rashi.eng: *small.* A small and despised kingdom, as he calls it above one small horn, and that is in the manner of (Obad. 1:2): “… you are very despised.”

rashi.heb:
*ותגדל יתר.* 
ותגדל מאד:
rashi.eng: *and it became very great.* Heb. וַתִּגְדַּל מְאֹד.

rashi.heb:
*אל הנגב.* 
הוא מצרים שהיא בדרומה של ארץ ישראל:
rashi.eng: *to the south.* That is Egypt, which is to the south of the land of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*ואל הצבי.* 
ארץ ישראל שנקראת ארץ צבי כענין שנאמר נחלת צבי צבאות גוים (ירמיהו ג׳:י״ט):
rashi.eng: *and to the coveted land.* Heb. הַצְבִי The land of Israel, called אֶרֶץ הַצְבִי, the coveted land [or the land of beauty] after the manner of (Jer. 3:19): “an inheritance of the beauty of hosts of nations.”

notes.448: (tn): Traditionally, “host.” The term refers to God’s heavenly angelic assembly, which he sometimes leads into battle as an army.
notes.449: (sn): In prescientific Israelite thinking the stars were associated with the angelic members of God’s heavenly assembly. See Judg 5:20; Job 38:7; Isa 40:26. In west Semitic mythology the stars were members of the high god’s divine assembly (see Isa 14:13).

rashi.heb:
*עד צבא השמים.* 
הם ישראל שנמשלו לכוכבים:
rashi.eng: *until the host of heaven.* They are Israel, who were compared to the stars.

notes.450: (sn): The prince of the army may refer to God (cf. “whose sanctuary” later in the verse) or to the angel Michael (cf. 12:1).
notes.451: (tn): Or perhaps “and by him,” referring to Antiochus rather than to God.
notes.452: (sn): Here the sanctuary is a reference to the temple of God in Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*ועד שר הצבא.* 
הוא בית המקדש שהוא ביתו של הקב"ה שר הצבא כלפי הקב"ה חרף: וממנו:
rashi.eng: *And until the Prince of the host.* That is the Temple, which is the House of the Holy One, blessed be He, the Prince of the host. He blasphemed the Holy One, blessed be He.

rashi.heb:
*הורם התמיד.* 
ועל ידי גדודיו וחילותיו ששלח לירושלים בטל התמיד ששלח שם נירון קיסר שר צבאו כמ"ש רז"ל במס' גטין ובגוריון:
rashi.eng: *and through him the daily sacrifice was removed.* And through his troops and his armies, which he sent to Jerusalem, the daily sacrifice was abolished, for he sent there Nero Caesar, his general, as our Rabbis relate in Gittin (56a) and in Gorion.

notes.453: (tc): The present translation reads וּצְבָאָהּ נִתַּן (uts�va’ah nittan) for the MT וְצָבָא תִּנָּתֵן (v�tsava’ tinnaten). The context suggests a perfect rather than an imperfect verb.
notes.454: (tn, Heb): “in (the course of) rebellion.” The meaning of the phrase is difficult to determine. It could mean “due to rebellion,” referring to the failures of the Jews, but this is not likely since it is not a point made elsewhere in the book. The phrase more probably refers to the rebellion against God and the atrocities against the Jews epitomized by Antiochus.
notes.455: (tc): Two medieval Hebrew MSS and the LXX have a passive verb here: “truth was hurled to the ground” (cf. NIV, NCV, TEV).
notes.456: (sn): Truth here probably refers to the Torah. According to 1 Macc 1:56, Antiochus initiated destruction of the sacred books of the Jews.

rashi.heb:
*וצבא תנתן על התמיד בפשע.* 
וזמן מועד נתן להיות התמיד מסולק בשביל פשע שומם היא ע"ג כלו' שתהא ע"ג נתנת בירושלים תמורת התמיד וכן היא קרויה בספר הזה בכמה מקומות שנא' עד מתי החזון התמיד והפשע שומם ואומר מעת הוסר התמיד ולתת שקוץ שומם:
rashi.eng: *And a time will be given for the daily sacrifice.* A set time will be given for the daily sacrifice to be discontinued because of transgression.

rashi.heb:
*וצבא.* 
זמן כמו הלא צבא לאנוש עלי ארץ (איוב ז):
rashi.eng: *And a time.* Heb. וְצָבָא, time, like (Job 7:1): “Is not man on Earth for a limited time (צָבָא)?”

rashi.heb:
*ותשלך אמת ארצה.* 
תורת אמת השפילה:
rashi.eng: *and it will cast truth to the Earth.* It humbled the Torah of truth.

notes.458: (sn): The holy one referred to here is presumably an angel. Cf. 4:13[10], 23 [20].

rashi.heb:
*אחד קדוש.* 
אחד מן המלאכים:
rashi.eng: *one holy one.* one of the angels.

rashi.heb:
*ויאמר.* 
אותו המלאך:
rashi.eng: *and… said.* that angel.

rashi.heb:
*לפלמוני.* 
הרי תיבה זו כשתים לפלוני אלמוני ותרגם יונתן בן עוזיאל בספר שמואל כסי וטמיר כמו כי יפלא ממך דבר, אלמוני אלמון מבלי שם שלא פי' לו מהו ומה שמו:
rashi.eng: *to the anonymous.* Heb. לַפַּלְמוֹנִי. This word is like two: פְּלוֹנִי אַלְמוֹנִי, and Jonathan ben Uziel translated it in the Book of Samuel (I 21:3): “covered and hidden,” like (Deut. 17:8): “If a matter be hidden (יִפָּלֵא) from you.” אַלְמוֹנִי means a widower (אַלְמָן) without a name, [i.e., bereft of a name] for he [the angel] did not explain to him what he was and what his name was.

rashi.heb:
*לפלמוני המדבר.* 
למלאך שהיה מדבר וגוזר גזירות וצבא המועד תנתן על התמיד בפשע:
rashi.eng: *to the anonymous one who was speaking.* to the angel who was speaking and issuing decrees, viz. “And a set time will be given for the daily sacrifice because of transgression.”

rashi.heb:
*עד מתי החזון.* 
הזה אשר על התמיד להיות מסולק והפשע השומם יהיה נתון תחתיו פשע שומם ע"א מעובדי כוכבים שהיא כאבן דומם וכן היא קרויה בספר הזה בכמה מקומות שנאמר עד מתי החזון התמיד והפשע שומם ואומר (לקמן יב) מעת הוסר התמיד ולתת שקוץ שומם:
rashi.eng: *How long will be the vision.* this [vision] which concerns the daily sacrifice, that it should be discontinued, and the silent abomination will be placed in its stead. The silent abomination is an idol worshipped by the pagans, which was like a mute stone, and so it is called in this Book in many places, as it says (12:11): “And from the time the daily sacrifice was removed and the silent abomination placed.”

rashi.heb:
*שומם.* 
ל' אלם ומשותק כמו אשתומם כשעה חדא (לעיל ג) ואשב שם שבעת ימים משמים בתוכם כמו אלם (יחזקאל ג׳:ט״ו):
rashi.eng: *mute.* Heb. שֹּׁמֵם, an expression of being mute and silenced, like (4:16): “was bewildered (אֶשְּׁתּוֹמַם) for awhile;” (Ezek. 3:15): “and I sat there seven days bewildered (מַשְּׁמִים) among them,” like one who is dumb.

rashi.heb:
*תת וקדש וצבא מרמס.* 
לתת את מכון המקדש ואת צבא השמים אשר הפיל לארץ מרמס לרגליו כמו שכתוב למעלה ותפל ארצה מן הצבא ומן הכוכבים:
rashi.eng: *permitting the Sanctuary and the host to be trampled.* to make the base of the Sanctuary and the host of heaven, which he cast down to the Earth, to be a trampling for his feet, as is stated above (verse 10): “and it cast down to the ground some of the host and some of the stars.”

rashi.heb:
*וקדש וצבא.* 
וי"ו יתירה והרבה כאלה במקרא נרדם ורכב וסוס (תהילים ע״ו:ז׳) ואף בלשון בני אדם יש מדברים כן:
rashi.eng: *the Sanctuary and the host.* Heb. וְצָבָא וְקֹדֶשּׁ. The “vav” [of וְקֹדֶשּׁ] is superfluous, and there are many such instances in Scripture, e.g. (Ps. 76:7): “chariot (וָרֶכֶב) and horse were stunned,” and also, in the language of people, some speak that way.

notes.459: (sn): The language of evenings and mornings is reminiscent of the creation account in Genesis 1. Since “evening and morning” is the equivalent of a day, the reference here would be to 2,300 days. However, some interpreters understand the reference to be to the evening sacrifice and the morning sacrifice, in which case the reference would be to only 1,150 days. Either way, the event that marked the commencement of this period is unclear. The event that marked the conclusion of the period is the rededication of the temple in Jerusalem following the atrocious and sacrilegious acts that Antiochus implemented. This took place on December 25, 165 B.C. The Jewish celebration of Hanukkah each year commemorates this victory.
notes.460: (tn, Heb): “will be vindicated” or “will be justified.” This is the only occurrence of this verb in the Niphal in the OT. English versions interpret it as “cleansed” (KJV, ASV), “restored” (NASB, TEV, NLT), or “reconsecrated” (NIV).

rashi.heb:
*עד ערב בקר אלפים ושלוש מאות.* 
ראיתי פתר בשם רבינו סעדיה לדבר וכבר עבר ופתר עוד עד ערב בקר עד שיבוא אותו הערב שנאמר בו והיה לעת ערב יהיה אור ובטוחים אנו כי דבר אלהינו יקום לעולם לא יופר ואני אומר כי הערב והבוקר האמור כאן גמטריא הוא ויש סמך לדבר משני טעמים האחד שיהא חשבון זה מכוון עם חשבון אחר שבסוף הספר, והב' שאמר גבריאל לדניאל למטה בענין ומראה הערב והבקר אשר נאמר אמת היא, ואם לא רמז החשבון הוא תלוי למה חזר וכפל אותו לומר אמת הוא, והחוזה נצטוה לסתום ולחתום הדבר ואף הוא לא נגלה בל' סתום וחתום ואנו נוחיל להבטחת מלכנו קץ אחר קץ ובעבור קץ הדורש נודע כי טעה במדרשיו, והבא אחריו יתור וידרוש דרך אחרת יש לפתור ערב ובקר בגי' ה' מאות ושבעי' וארבע ועוד אלפי' ושלש מאות הרי אלפים וח' מאות וע"ד:
rashi.eng: *Until evening and morning, two thousand and three hundred.* I saw an interpretation in the name of Rav Saadia Gaon for this matter, but it has already passed, and he interpreted further “until evening and morning,” that evening about which it says (Zech. 14:7): “and it shall come to pass that at eventide it shall be light,” and we are confident that our God’s word will stand forever; it will not be nullified. I say, however, that the עֶרֶב and בֹּקֶר stated here are a gematria, and there is support for this matter from two reasons: 1) that this computation should coincide with the other computation at the end of the Book, and 2) that Gabriel said to Daniel later on in this chapter (verse 26): “And the vision of the evening and the morning is true.” Now, if he had not hinted that the computation was doubtful, why did he repeat it to say that it was true? And the seer was commanded to close up and to seal the matter, and to him, too, the matter was revealed in a closed and sealed expression, but we will hope for the promise of our king for end after end, and when the end passes, it will be known that the expounder has erred in his interpretation, and the one who comes after him will search and expound in another manner. This can be interpreted [as follows]: namely, that עֶרֶב בֹּקֶר has the numerical value of 574, ע = 70; ר = 200; ב = 2; ב = 2; ק = 100; ר = 200. Added together, this equals 574; plus 2,300, we have 2,874.

rashi.heb:
*ונצדק קדש.* 
יכופר עון ישראל לבטל גזרות מדרסן ומרפסן מאז גלו גלות ראשונה למצרים עד יגאלו ויושעו תשועת עולמים במלך משיחנו וחשבון זה כלה לסוף אל"ף ור"ץ מיום הוסר התמיד והוא שנאמר בסוף הספר ומעת הוסר התמיד כדי לתת שיקוץ שומ' ימים אלף ור"ץ יהיה ולא יותר שיבא המלך משיחנו ויסיר שקוץ השומם והתמיד הוסר ו' שנים לפני החורבן ב"ש והעמיד צלם בהיכל ויום י"ז בתמוז היה ששרף אפוסטמוס את התורה ובטל את התמיד והעמיד צלם בהיכל כמו ששנינו במסכת תענית, ושש שנים שכתבתי אין בידי ראיה מפורשת אך יש ראיה ששבוע שלם לא בטל התמיד לפני החורבן שכן ניבא דניאל על טיטוס (לקמן ט') וחצי השבוע ישבית זבח ומנחה כלומר מקצת השבוע שלפני החורבן יבטלו הקרבנו' כך מפורש למטה בענין נחזור על הראשונו' כיצד מכוון חשבון ערב ובקר אלפי' ושלש מאות מיום רדת ישראל למצרים להיות כלה לסוף אלף ור"ץ ליום שהוסר התמיד, ר"י היו במצרים ד' מאות ושמונים מיום צאתם עד ויבן הבית ד' מאו' וי' היה הבית וע' שנה גלות בבל וד' מאות וך' בית שני תן עליהם אלף ור"ץ של קץ הימים הרי אלפים וח' מאות צא מהן ו' שנים שהוסר התמיד לפני החורבן שלא מנה הכתוב אלף ור"ץ אלא למעת הוסר התמיד הרי לך חשבון ערב ובוקר ואלפים וג' מאות עוד נוסף בחשבון אשרי המחכה ויגיע לקץ הימים מ"ה שנה יתרים על אלף ור"ץ יש לומר על חשבון הראשון יצא המלך המשיח ויחזור ויתכסה מהם אותם מ"ה שנים ורבי אליעזר הקליר יסד (בסילוק יוצר של פרשת החדש) ביסוד שירו שבועים ששה הרי מ"ב, וי"ל הג' שנים שלא באו לחשבון שבוע לא מנה ואני מצאתי כך במדרש רות שעתיד מלך המשיח להתכסות מ"ה שנים לאחר שיגלה ומביא ראיה מן המקראות הללו:
rashi.eng: *and the holy ones shall be exonerated.* The iniquity of Israel shall be expiated to bring an end to the decrees of their being trodden upon and crumbled since they were exiled in their first exile to Egypt, until they will be redeemed and saved with a perpetual salvation by our king Messiah, and this computation terminates at the end of 1, 290 years from the day the daily sacrifice was removed, and that is what is stated at the end of the Book (12:11): “And from the time the daily sacrifice is removed, and the silent abomination placed, will be 1,290 years,” and no more, for our king Messiah will come and remove the silent abomination. The daily sacrifice was removed six years before the destruction of the Second Temple, and an image was set up in the Heichal. Now that was the seventeenth day of Tammuz, when Apostomos burned the Torah, put an end to the daily sacrifice, and set up an image in the Heichal, as we learned in Tractate Ta’anith (26b), but for the six years that I mentioned, I have no explicit proof, but there is proof that the daily sacrifice was abolished less than a complete shemittah cycle before the destruction, for so did Daniel prophesy about Titus (9:27): “… and half the week of years [shemittah cycle] he will curtail sacrifice and meal-offering,” meaning that a part of the week of years before the destruction, sacrifices will be abolished. So it is explained below in this section. Let us return to the earlier matters, how the computation of “evening and morning, two thousand and three hundred,” fits exactly with the time commencing from the descent to Egypt to terminate at the end of 1,290 years until the day that the daily sacrifice was abolished: 210 years they were in Egypt. 480 years transpired from the Exodus until the building of the Temple. 410 years the Temple existed. 70 years was the Babylonian exile. 420 years the Second Temple stood. 1,290 should be added until the end of days, totaling: 2,880. Subtract six years that the daily sacrifice was removed before the destruction, for Scripture counted 1,290 years only from the time that the daily sacrifice was removed. Here you have the computation of “evening and morning, and 2,300” added to the computation. Fortunate is he who waits and reaches the end of days 45 years over 1,290 [years]. We may say that the king Messiah will come according to the first computation, and he will subsequently be concealed from them for forty-five years. Rabbi Elazar HaKalir established (in the concluding poem of the portion dealing with the month of Nissan): in the foundation of his song: six weeks of years, totaling 42. We may say that the three years that did not total a week of years he did not count. And I found it so in Midrash Ruth that the king Messiah is destined to be concealed for forty-five years after he reveals himself, and proof is brought from these verses.

rashi.heb:
*ואבקשה בינה.* 
הייתי מתאוה שיבינו לי מן השמים:
rashi.eng: *that I sought understanding.* I was longing that they should enable me to understand [the vision] from heaven.

notes.461: (sn): The only angels whose names are given in the OT are Gabriel (Dan 8:16; 9:21; cf. Luke 1:19, 26) and Michael (Dan 10:13, 21; 12:1; cf. Jude 9; Rev 12:7). The name Gabriel means in Hebrew “man of God,” and Michael means “who is like God?”

rashi.heb:
*בין אולי.* 
בתוך הנהר:
rashi.eng: *in the midst of the Ulai.* in the midst of the river.

rashi.heb:
*ויקרא.* 
האדם:
rashi.eng: *and he called.* i.e., the man.

rashi.heb:
*ויאמר.* 
למלאך אתה גבריאל:
rashi.eng: *and said.* to the angel, “You, Gabriel.”

rashi.heb:
*הבן להלז את המראה.* 
פרש לזה את החזון:
rashi.eng: *enable this one to understand the vision.* explain the vision to this one.

rashi.heb:
*להלז.* 
לשון חשיבות כמו שקראו חמודות כל מקום שנא' הלז בעל צורה הוא ומכאן למדו באגדה יצחק נדמה לאביו בצלם ובדמות שנקרא האיש הלז בפ' ויהי כי זקן יצחק ויהי יוסף יפה תואר זהו הנוי המנוי בה' דברים שהאב זוכה לבנו:
rashi.eng: *this one.* Heb. לְהַלָּז, an expression of esteem, as he called him חֲמוּדוֹת, one of desirable qualities. Wherever it says הַלָז it refers to a person of form, and from here they learned in the Aggadah: Isaac resembled his father in form and in likeness, for he is called הָאִישּׁ הַלָז in the section commencing, “Now it came to pass when Isaac was old.” (Gen. 39: 6): “… and Joseph was fair in form and fair in appearance.” This is the beauty enumerated among the five things that a father merits for his son.

rashi.heb:
*לעת קץ.* 
לימים רבים יהיה החזון הזה:
rashi.eng: *to the time of the end..* For many days this vision will come about.

rashi.heb:
*נרדמתי.* 
ל' תנומה ושממון:
rashi.eng: *I fell into a sound sleep.* An expression of slumber and bewilderment.

rashi.heb:
*על עמדי.* 
על מעמד רגלי:
rashi.eng: *and stood me up where I had been standing.* Where my feet were standing.

notes.465: (tn): The Hebrew text does not actually state the referent (the vision Daniel saw in vv. 8-12; cf. also v. 13), which has been specified in the translation for clarity. Some Greek witnesses add “the vision” here.

rashi.heb:
*כי למועד קץ.* 
כי הוא לזמן קץ ימים רבים:
rashi.eng: *for it is the end of the time.* for it is at the time of the end of many days.

rashi.heb:
*מלכי מדי ופרס.* 
ב' קרנים שתי אומות מולכות כמו שפירשתי למעלה:
rashi.eng: *The kings of Media and Persia.* The two horns represent two ruling nations, as I explained above.

notes.466: (tn, Heb): “the he-goat, the buck.” The expression is odd, and the second word may be an explanatory gloss.

rashi.heb:
*המלך הראשון.* 
הוא אלכסנדרוס מוקדן שהרג את דריוש בן אסתר כמו שמצינו בספר יוסיפון:
rashi.eng: *the first king.* He is Alexander of Macedon who slew Darius, the son of Esther, as we find in the book of Josiphon (ch. 9).

notes.468: (tn, Heb): “the broken one.” The word “horn” has been supplied in the translation to clarify the referent.

rashi.heb:
*והנשברת.* 
שראית שנשברה:
rashi.eng: *And the broken one.* that you saw being broken.

rashi.heb:
*ותעמודנה ארבע תחתיה.* 
כמו שכתוב בספור החלום למעלה: ד' מלכיות, אשר יעמודנה מאותו גוי שחלק אלכסנדרוס מוקדן מלכותו במותו לארבע ילדים ויוסף קראם בספרו ארבע ראשי נמר ולא בני המלך היו:
rashi.eng: *in whose stead stood four.* as is written in the narration of the dream above (verse 8), [there] are four kingdoms which will arise from that nation, for Alexander of Macedon divided his kingdom upon his death [into parts for] four youths, and Joseph called them four heads of a leopard in his book, and they were not the sons of the king.

rashi.heb:
*ולא בכחו.* 
ולא יהיו האחרונים ככח המלך הראשון כי חלשים ממנו יהיו:
rashi.eng: *but not with its strength.* The last ones will not be as strong as the first king, but they will be weaker than him.

notes.469: (tc): The present translation reads הַפְּשָׁעִים (happ�sha’im, “rebellious acts”) for the MT הַפֹּשְׁעִים (happosh�’im, “rebels”). While the MT is understandable (cf. NIV, “when rebels have become completely wicked”), the filling up of transgressions is a familiar OT expression (cf. Gen 15:16) and fits this context well. Cf. the LXX, Theodotion, the Vulgate, and the Syriac.
notes.471: (tn, Heb): “understanding riddles.” Possible meanings include “double-dealing” (BDB 295 s.v. חִידָה; cf. TEV, CEV) and “with a good knowledge of intrigue” (HALOT 309 s.v. חִידָה; cf. NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*ובאחרית מלכותם כהתם הפושעים.* 
כשיגיעו זמן שיתמו רשעי ישראל שבבית שני:
rashi.eng: *And at the end of their kingdom, when the transgressors have been destroyed.* When the end arrives, and the wicked of Israel in the Second Temple will be finished.

rashi.heb:
*יעמוד מלך עז פנים.* 
הוא טיטוס:
rashi.eng: *a brazen-faced person will rise.* he is Titus.

notes.475: (tn): See the corresponding Aramaic expression in 7:27. If the “holy ones” are angels, then this probably refers to the angels as protectors of God’s people. One could translate, “people belonging to (i.e., protected by) the holy ones.” If the “holy ones” are God’s people, then this is an appositional construction, “the people who are the holy ones.” One could translate simply “holy people.” For examples of a plural appositional genitive after “people,” see 11:15, 32. Because either interpretation is possible, the translation has deliberately preserved the ambiguity of the Hebrew grammar here.

rashi.heb:
*ועצם כחו.* 
ולא בגבורה כי אם בחלקלקות כמו שמפורש בסוף הספר:
rashi.eng: *And his power will become strong.* and not with might but with smooth talk, as is explained at the end of the Book (11: 21).

rashi.heb:
*ונפלאות ישחית.* 
ובהפלא ופלא ישחית עובדי כוכבים:
rashi.eng: *and he will destroy wondrously.* and with wonder upon wonder, he will destroy.

rashi.heb:
*והצליח ועשה.* 
חפצו:
rashi.eng: *and he will prosper and accomplish.* his desire.

rashi.heb:
*והשחית עצומים.* 
השחית אומות רבות:
rashi.eng: *and he will destroy the mighty.* many nations.

rashi.heb:
*ועם קדושים.* 
ישראל המאמינים בתורה:
rashi.eng: *and the people of the holy ones.* Israel, who believe in the Torah.

notes.476: (tn): The Hebrew term has a primary meaning of “skill, insight,” but here it has the connotation “cunning, treachery.” See BDB 968 s.v. שֵׂכֶל, שֶׂכֶל.
notes.477: (tn, Heb): “he will cause deceit to succeed by his hand.”
notes.478: (tn, Heb): “in his heart he will act arrogantly.”
notes.479: (tn, Heb): “in peace.” The Hebrew word used here is difficult. It may refer to the security felt by those who did not realize the danger of imminent attack, or it may refer to the condition of being unaware of the impending danger. The latter idea is reflected in the present translation. See further, BDB 1017 s.v. שַׁלְוָה.

rashi.heb:
*ועל שכלו והצליח מרמה בידו.* 
ועל ידי שהוא משכיל בכל אשר יפנה ויצליח יחזיק במרמה שבידו:
rashi.eng: *And through his intellect, he will cause the deceit in his hand to prosper.* And because he is clever wherever he turns and [because] he will prosper, he will hold onto deceit with his hand.

rashi.heb:
*ובלבבו יגדיל.* 
יתגאה:
rashi.eng: *and in his heart he will become proud.* Heb. יַגְדִּיל, lit, he will grow larger.

rashi.heb:
*ובשלוה ישחית רבים.* 
במרמה ובחלקלקות ישחית רבים היושבים אתו בברית ושלום:
rashi.eng: *and in tranquility he will destroy many.* With guile and with smooth talk he will destroy many who dwell with him with a covenant and in peace.

rashi.heb:
*ועל שר שרים יעמוד.* 
כלפי מעלה יטיח דברים זהו פירוש החלום הכתוב למעלה (ועד שר הצבא הגדיל):
rashi.eng: *and over the Prince of princes he will stand.* He will speak blasphemously about Heaven. This is the meaning of the dream written above (verse 11): [“And until the Prince of the host it grew.”]

rashi.heb:
*ובאפס יד ישבר.* 
ובאין כח ישבר ע"י יתוש חלש שבבריות שנכנס בחוטמו כמו ששנינו במסכת גיטין:
rashi.eng: *and without strength he will be broken.* And without strength he will be broken, through a mosquito, the weakest of creatures, which entered his nose, as we learned in Tractate Gittin (56b).

rashi.heb:
*ומראה הערב והבקר.* 
אשר נאמר לך בחלום העליון אמת הוא:
rashi.eng: *And the vision of the evening and the morning.* which was said to you in the preceding dream, is true.

rashi.heb:
*ואתה סתום החזון.* 
אל תפרשהו וסתמהו בלבך כי לימים רבים יבא:
rashi.eng: *and you close up the vision.* Do not explain it, but close it up in your heart, for it will come about in many days.

notes.482: (tn): The Hebrew word here is נִהְיֵיתִי (nihyetiy). Its meaning is not entirely clear. Hebrew הָיָה (hayah) normally has meanings such as “to be” or “become.” Here, however, it describes Daniel’s emotional and physical response to the enigmatic vision that he has seen. It is parallel to the following verb, which refers to illness, and seems to refer to a state of utter exhaustion due to the amazing things that Daniel has just seen. The LXX lacks the word. On the meaning of the word see further, BDB 227-28 s.v. הָיָה Niph.2; DCH 2:540 s.v. היה I Ni.3.

rashi.heb:
